utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, please, my name is Niemann. I appear with my colleagues, Ms. McHenry, Mr. Turone and Mr. Huber, for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Appearances for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, I am Edina Residovic, Defence counsel for Mr. Zejnil Delalic. Mr. Delalic is also represented by my colleague, Eugene O'Sullivan, professor from Canada.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, I am Mr. Olujic, defence counsel for Mr. Mucic, along with my colleague, Niko Duric, attorney from Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, I am Salih Karabdic, attorney from Sarajevo, defence counsel for Mr. Hazim Delic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I am Nancy Boler. I represent Esad Landzo, I am from Houston, Texas. With me today is Ken Lindsey, also from Houston, Texas, who is now the legal assistant for our Defence team. Cynthia McMurrey will not be in the courtroom today. She is busy with other Defence matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: May we have the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, before the witness comes in, may I raise a matter. It relates to the provision of the witness list for the witnesses of Mr. Delalic. Our witness list has only got three names on it at the moment, and we have written to the Defence for Mr. Delalic. We assume that these three witnesses will be expired by Friday, and we don't think they will take any longer than that. I understand that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I hope they don't expire.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Perhaps that's -- we'll complete them. Your Honours, I understand that an appeal is being lodged, that that shouldn't interfere with Your Honours orders, as far as I understand it, and that Your Honours orders will apply at least up and until any decision to the contrary is made. We depend very heavily, Your Honours, on these lists to prepare ourselves for cross-examination and, we can only assume that there is going to be a further batch of witnesses next Monday, that will start next Monday and run through. We don't know who they are, and we don't seem to be able to persuade the Defence for Mr. Delalic to give us the list, and we would ask Your Honours to encourage them to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: As far as the Trial Chamber is concerned, we tend to carry on through next week with the list you have, because I think we had sufficient time within which to get these witnesses here. I will make provision for that, on being examined and cross-examined. If you received the Notice of Appeal --

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: We don't, you see. Your Honour gets the full list, but we don't. They only give us the lists of the witnesses they have called in the next seven days, so our list has only got three names on it, ending with Mr. Milic, and there it ends. And they won't give it to us unless --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Until they are sure they are calling the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That's somewhat a disadvantage to us, Your Honour, because the position at the moment is that they are simply not going to call any witnesses, as I understand, next week, but if they do comply with Your Honours orders, which we must assume they will do, by Monday they will commence to call witnesses, and we won't know who they were and we will have had no time to prepare.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I suppose they will comply.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, I suspect they'll comply, and therefore, I ask Your Honour to encourage them to comply with the other order, and that is to give us the matters. Your Honours have already got the list of witnesses. We don't have them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just must say, before I call the witness, that the Defence, regardless of all the efforts that it is making, is not going to be able to call the witnesses that were called for the 22nd. They are professionally engaged. They are not in Bosnia. They are only coming back on 20th July. They are all archive specialists, and the only way that I can see out is to issue a subpoena for their presence. So it is not in our power to get them here before the 20th of July. This is what we were trying to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: July or June? Are you talking about July or June 22nd?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You've been using the word "July".

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: They are very similar words, so sometimes it may be misinterpreted. We have -- regardless of all the efforts that we've been making, we cannot bring them. We brought witnesses from Austria, from Germany, everybody that we could get, and there are people who have professional obligations in the US So we really cannot do that. They are coming back on the 17th or 18th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: This is not an issue before us now. We've already rejected your application and made an order. So that is not an issue here. Will you kindly lead your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, to interrupt. It's no help for us to tell us that they can't get them here. Your Honour has made an order and they really do need to tell us. There is no reason why they shouldn't tell us. I mean, they know who they are. There is no secret about who they are. So I do -- I will file something, if necessary, which I'll proceed to do today, seeking a direct order from Your Honours to compel them to comply. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Okay -- they are disobeying the order. Carry on with your witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I remind you, sir, that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, General.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you been able to rest from yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, yesterday it happened that the question and answer overlapped and the interpreters were unable to fully interpret everything that I asked and everything that you answered. So again let me remind you, please wait for the entire question to be asked, and only then, after it's been interpreted, answer it. Is that clear, sir?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you will recall that yesterday, before the afternoon recess, we talked about the appointment of Mr. Zejnil Delalic dated 27 July 1992. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also recall that you said that this appointment was vague and unimplementable. General, can you tell me, in a situation when a similar kind of order would appear, would the authorities, who are responsible for certain duties of this kind, correct these mistakes, and did this also happen in 1992, that they would do this?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes. At any rate, when any kind of mistake would be identified in any kind of document or order, and this would be an obstacle to its implementation, it would immediately be corrected. In other words, another order would be issued which would cancel the previous order, or the parts of those -- that previous order which were vague or unclear.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to request that the General be shown the Exhibit D146/1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, do you have in front of you the order for disposition of 8 August 1992 issued by the President of Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Mr. Alija Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, I do have that order in front of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, if you have the English version of this order, to please place it on the ELMO. General, can you please tell me from this order for disposition, paragraph 1, it states that Zejnil Delalic is assigned to commander of Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, you can clearly see from this order that Zejnil Delalic is being appointed to the formation post of commander of Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, will you now please look at paragraph 2 of this order for disposition. Can you please read it and explain what it means to you.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, I can. According to wartime formation of the competent commanders -- (no translation)

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Hold on. May the witness please repeat the answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, the interpretation stops. Let me ask you to repeat the answer. Just reread paragraph 2. It has not been read. And for the sake of the interpreters, please do it slowly.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. "According to the wartime formation, the authorised heads of units and headquarters, which had been anticipated in this order, will cancel all their previous orders of disposition and appointment of officers, which are included in this order."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. General, if formally an order -- the order of 27 July is existed, has it been made null and void, that is cancelled by this order?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Obviously, that is the case, because in the order of 27th, Zejnil Delalic is also mentioned, as well as the Tactical Group, and we already commented on this order. I am certain that the responsible persons did see the mistake in that order, and that they responded as fast as they could in order to correct the error and, as a result, this order was written which cancels the previous order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Before this Tribunal you testified that you were appointed commander of Tactical Group 1 on 12 May 1992. You also testified that your deputy, that is your chief of staff, was Sucro Pilica. General, could you personally appoint your own chief of staff?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: No, I did not have such authority, and I could not appoint -- I could not appoint chief of staff of the Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who could appoint chief of staff in the Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: The chief of staff could have been appointed the chief of staff of the supreme command or a person whom he authorised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would now like to request that the next document be marked, be given to the witness, and I have a sufficient number of copies for the court.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Defence document D183/1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, is this person, Sucro Pilica, the person who was appointed as your deputy in the Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes. This is Sucro Pilica, who was chief of staff of the Tactical Group 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, I am not going to try to introduce this document into evidence through you, but I would like to ask whether you can say, is -- at the top of this document is there a title "forward command post", that is the section of the main staff which was in Visoko?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, that is what is indicated here. It is the forward section of the supreme command staff which was operating in Visoko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, is this a part of the main staff to which you transferred after you turned over your duty in the Tactical Group to Mr. Zejnil Delalic?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, that is the staff that you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, do you know that this forward command post of the main staff was authorised by the main staff in Sarajevo to conduct certain affairs on behalf of the main staff?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes. The supreme staff did transfer certain authority to its forward post, which was active in Visoko. Among others, the commander of this part of the staff, Mr. Rasim Delic, is now commander of the joint armed forces of the federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, did receive such authority and acted accordingly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, General, you yourself could not, on your own, appoint your deputy, but, General, as the commander of the Tactical Group, were you able to appoint members of your staff, of your command?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: No. The members of the command of the Tactical Group were appointed by the members of the supreme command staff, and this is what you can see in this document where, beside the deputy, the chief of staff, assistant officer for logistics, Mustafa Gagula was also appointed.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, there is a problem with the transcript, on page 9. It says Mr. Zejnil Delalic. I believe the witness said Mr. Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: That's correct. It should be corrected. That's correct. It's an error in translation. Or interpretation, I would say.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, it is Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think it's in the interpretation. Rasim Delic did not appear on the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: To be of assistance, it's Rasim, R-A-S-I-M.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Rasim Delic, who is the current commander of the joint armed forces of the federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May the General now please be shown the Prosecution exhibit number 193?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I don't know where all of this is leading to, what this is leading to. Does Council hear me? I don't know what all of this is leading to.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We are trying to determine the authorities and responsibilities of commander of Tactical Group. The Prosecution has offered a document of which I am trying to show the witness now, which allegedly talks about Mr. Delalic's authorities and time within which he did that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: -- evidence on this, three earlier witnesses, on the authority of the Tactical Group commander. And the Prosecution, actually, did -- that is not enough. All the witnesses who are members of the army to come and tell everyone coming to say the same thing. It's not sufficient. That's not the way to lead evidence. You've had enough of the authority of the commander of the Tactical Group, what it can do, what it cannot do. They have said several times.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have heard certain things, for example, on the expert, but this is a commander, and nobody can explain that better to the Chamber who is only interested in truth. Nobody can tell us more about the authorities of the commander of Tactical Group back in 1992, and the previous two documents shown have not been shown to any other witness. This one was shown by the Prosecution, that is true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The last witness was called on the ground that he worked with the Tactical Group 1 commander. That was one of the grounds. He was chief of staff. He knew of the powers, exercise of authority of that officer. What type of evidence is that?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is the essence of the indictment. I asked my client, we have eliminated many questions, we are not talking about the war or the siege and conditions, we are only dealing with the authorities. And this is the only burden of proof of indictments against my witness -- sorry, against my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: This is a document by which Delalic made a lot -- number of appointments and you want to show that he was not competent to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, I would wish this witness would testify to that because at the time of the issue of this order, he was still a commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: This is what you wanted this witness to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But I cannot say that. This can only be told to you by this witness, if he knows that, because I am not before this Court as a witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, I suppose you've never seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: How could he see it, he was not there then.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I just said that. I presume he has never seen it. I would only be interested if this witness could look at the date of issue of this order or this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When has this document been issued, General?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: It states the 18th of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell this Chamber who was TG-1 commander at the time?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: I have already said that, it was myself. And from what I can see here, this document recalls the order of the July 11th, 1992, which we have also commented yesterday and we determined that this order had never been implemented. When I was a TG commander at that time, no one else could write an order on my behalf, that is as a TG-1 commander. Whilst here I see a number of people, and I have said specifically how many people counted in the command of the tactical group and, according to this document, I don't think this would be the true state shown on the document. I have also never seen it. I did not know of its existence. It could be possible this has been even falsified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Just one minute. I just don't understand one thing. In this document, which is much earlier, 18th of July, I think. He described himself as a TG commander. According to this witness, he took over as a TG commander on the 29th of July, so how could Delalic describe himself as a tactical commander much before the order with regard to the appointment was received in Konjic? I just don't understand that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are trying to prove that Delalic never wrote this. This Prosecution claims the existence of this document because Delalic has no clue of the existence of it. That's why I needed this witness to testify that he was a commander then and there was no chance that somebody be in his position. For that reason, it was necessary to prove that because we have all sorts of documents during the war. And this witness, who knows this from his personal experience, can testify here, which he did yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: But was this document found in papers recovered from INDA-BAU?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: No. This is an inauthentic document, but the Prosecution has shown it to at least ten witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Just carry on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And we believe that this is not an authentic document.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Before we carry on, further point in the transcript, page 11, line 21. I believe my learned college, Ms. Residovic, asked for Prosecution Exhibit 193 and the transcript says 123. For the sake of clarity, could we say 193, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. May this document be returned to the file. I have asked the questions that I intended to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you have spoken yesterday about the attempts you made to lift the siege and we also had units from Konjic participating, can you tell us what was the first time when units from Konjic were subordinated to your command?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: For the first time, Konjic units were subordinated to TG-1 on June 12th, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who issued an order about the subordination of those units to you in Pazaric?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: A written order was written by the main staff of the supreme command for all the units participating in the operation and, specifically, the order for that particular unit to be transferred from the municipal staff of Konjic was issued by the municipal staff commander in Konjic at that time, Ramic Esad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, at the time of subordination of that unit to you, did you have any knowledge that Mr. Delalic had any military or command function in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: No, I do not know of that. I do not have knowledge of Delalic's function in Konjic at that time or any other place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know at that time that the war presidency appointed him coordinator?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Personally, no, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: But how is he concerned with that?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: He have knowledge of Gajret who could possibly know whether Zejnil Delalic has any tasks or functions connected to that unit and that's what I wanted to ask of him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: I said I did have some knowledge as concerns logistical support of that unit from the municipal staff of Konjic, Mr. Delalic helped in the supply and I know that this was the best equipped unit which came to Tactical Group 1 at that time, so he helped in the equipping of this unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you have mentioned yesterday that at instances you would transmit the supreme command's orders to other staffs and commanders. Can you tell us, during 1992, was this a common practice for commanders who were outside of the city under siege to be used to transmit orders of the main staff?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, this was common practice. And myself as a TG commander was in a position to transmit orders of the supreme command staff to other commanders.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now ask that this witness be shown documents D-145, Annex 5/41, page 113 and D-145, Annex 5 D-45, page 818. Could you please take the order dated 24th August and put the English version on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You obtained the opinion of the expert and other witnesses on this document. Would the opinion of this witness further strengthen your case on that? He was not directly concerned with this order. He had said that the supreme command being posted in the places under siege, thought whatever means were convenient to convey messages to other commanders, would his opinion further strengthen your opinion in that? We have the opinion of the military expert on this, you even asked Mr. Asim, the last witness on, this, why do you keep on repeating? I just don't understand. He's not directly concerned with this document. If he had been directly concerned, you're quite justified in questioning him with regard to this document. He's not directly concerned. Is what my learned friend Gosimer is telling you, don't duplicate, don't triplicate, don't quadruplicate the same evidence, particularly when it relates to a matter of opinion, essentially.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If Your Honours find this fact clarified enough --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He's going to say exactly the same as the other witnesses have said. How does it help your case?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The number of witnesses do not clarify a thing. It doesn't how many witnesses you call, if it's matters of skill, it remains of skill. There are issues which counsel will refer to in submissions on the last date. We really do not require extra evidence, other than what you already have on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: It's not the number of witnesses which prove a point, it's the quality of evidence. If he had been directly concerned with this document, you are quite justified in asking him. But he's not personally concerned with this document. You are mainly asking him his opinion.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, having in mind the Prosecution asked opinion on one of the same documents several times, I tried to do the same. But since you are telling me that this is the third time we're dealing with this document, then maybe this witness shouldn't give his opinion on these documents as well. But I still, nevertheless, think that his opinion may have an influence on the evidence. This is the only witness who could give us a point of view of a commander of a tactical group. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, connected with the things you have mentioned about the practice during the war, in the transmission of the supreme command orders, would you at that time rely on, or refer to, the authority given to you by the supreme command to transmit such orders?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, this is common practice with transmission of orders, to refer to the order of the command that issued it. Instances where this was not done, the original copy of the order would then be sent out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I apologise, but I am trying to follow your directions, Your Honour, so I will try to skip over some questions that may have been answered by some other witnesses. General, yesterday you said that as a TG commander, you did not have authority over institutions, in your personal knowledge and experience, did at any given moment, Tactical Group 1 had been given or took over had the authority of district staffs of that area?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: No, TG had never had any authority, including the territorial powers in the area, but only over those units which were subordinated to us for a specific combat task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, whilst you were the commander and later, according to your knowledge as a member of the forward command post of Visoko, did tactical group have any authorities of the corps?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: No, we had no authority of that type. This was exclusively a combat group, not even an unit. And we did not have any special authority, apart from the one to perform the task given and that is to try to lift the siege of Sarajevo in the area mentioned aforehand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, General, during your command of a tactical group and later on as a member of staff of a member of command of the forward command post, did you ever gain knowledge of an existence of a prison or punishments of military personnel within the area of the Municipality of Konjic?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: No, something of the sort has never been under the authority of the tactical group, including me as a commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you as a commander of tactical group and a member of the forward command post of Visoko ever give certain authorities to a commander of a tactical group referring to the prison of Celebici or concerning the punishment of people in that prison facility?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: May I ask a question? General, you were TG commander 1 and you went to the formations, did you take any prisoners yourself, your units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, tactical group never had any prisons and it did not have any type of a collection centre or staff building or anything connected to that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The counsel should turn off their microphone while conferring.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Concerning your testimony about you transmitting orders to certain municipal staffs, can you tell us if that particular task of transmitting orders at the same time gave you any authority over those municipal staffs?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: No, they had not given me any authority, this was just my obligation to transmit orders and I had no further authority as a TG commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your testifying yesterday, you have said that and you repeated even today, that final orders of which units are to be subordinated to you were issued by heads of municipal staffs. In addition to the man power to be subordinated to you, did commanders of municipal staffs, following the order of the main staff, have any other obligations, for example, to provide those units with logistics and equipment or information or intelligence, rather?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Tactical group did not have separate logistics elements in its formations. And this was one of the tasks of the Territorial Defence. The units which would be subordinated to the tactical group needed to be equipped by the TO for the forthcoming operation. Also, the tactical group was also obliged to forward any reconnaissance or intelligence information within their area to give for use. The TO was obliged to give such information to the tactical group, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These information by the enemy, were they important for the conduct of the task before the TG?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Any soldier can tell you that this is the crucial part, the most important one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a commander of tactical group, could you in that light ask of them to forward to you anything connected to such information?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: This was necessary due to a lack of reconnaissance within the tactical group, so we had to rely on the units of the TO for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would now ask the witness be shown the exhibit for the Prosecution. Just a moment until I find its designation. 224. Could you place the English version on the ELMO, please. I presume, General, that you have not seen this document?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does such an order issued by the commander of a TG stem out of his right to gather intelligence for the purpose of the conduct of his task?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: I know that TO staffs, according to a directive from the main staff, had an obligation to perform this duty of providing intelligence to the tactical group concerning the enemy situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you now take a look of the paragraph 6 of this order. I will now ask you a hypothetical question. Had you written this order, using this formulation of the responsibility of the municipal staff commanders to provide you with information, would it have been possible for you to punish a municipal staff commander for not meeting this requirement?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: No, I have said that municipal staffs, with their commanders, are obliged to provide information on the enemy to the tactical group. I suppose that this task was not done properly. They did not provide information on time and those informations were not valid and that the then commander of the tactical group was forced to warn them of that, reminding them of their obligation to meet their duties. No authority concerning command or superior authority, including punishment, tactical commander group cannot be the person to command or punish commanders of municipal staffs. The only thing that he can do is to report the main staff of the supreme command about the commanders of municipal staffs not meeting the requirement. And all the measures to be taken fall under the authority of the supreme command staff or the superior command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, the Court has heard from several witnesses what were the logistics problem in the army and in which way the materiel was acquired. Do you personally know that both the military and civilian authorities did authorise persons to provide a certain equipment or other means necessary for the defence?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes. This was one of the main sources of the logistics of all our formations. Taking into account the situation in which we found ourselves in the Territorial Defence, that is in our armed forces, and in our -- in the overall structure of our society, anyone who could in any way contribute and assist the population and defence, and who was engaged in that, did receive authority from the -- the competent authorities in order to engage in such activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, if you were in a situation to give authority to either a business person or another civilian to acquire certain materiel, did such person acquire a status of a military person?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May the witness please be shown the document D145-9/7. It's page 993, which the Prosecutor yesterday showed another witness. Will you also place the English version on the ELMO, sir. I believe that the English version is already on the ELMO. This is a Power of Attorney to Zejnil Delalic, signed by Minister Jerko Doko for acquisition of materiel dated 9 May 1992. Is this what you see in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, that is -- even though the body of text is barely legible, but I can see Jerko Doko's signature at the bottom, and I also do see the date of 9 May 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, is this one of the usual powers -- Power of Attorneys, they had different forms, but the essence is the same, it empowers somebody to acquire certain materiel for the needs of defence?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes. This is one of the usual documents in this particular case issued by the Minister of Defence, Mr. Jerko Doko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With this respect I have a question, that this power also gives this person any military authority?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: This authorisation does not give any authorities with respect to the military service. The person is only authorised to acquire and procure and bring these means to the persons or institutions who had authorised them to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, when during 1992 did you meet Mr. Zejnil Delalic?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: I met Zejnil Delalic for the first time during the preparation for the first lifting -- attempted lifting of the siege of Sarajevo, when I was looking for support in materiel for this operation. And it was at that time that we first met and became acquainted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you have testified before the Tribunal that as commander of Tactical Group you visited the different municipalities and in order to see what units were available for the Tactical Group. Can you tell me, do you know from your personal experience whether Mr. Zejnil Delalic was commander of the municipal staff in Konjic during this period?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: It is absolutely correct, that while I was commander of the Tactical Group, Zejnil Delalic was not commander of the municipal staff -- of the Territorial Defence of Konjic, and I know that he was not that later either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, did Defence for Mr. Zejnil Delalic in May, 1996, come in touch with you, at this time you were commander of the fourth corps of the BiH army, to provide information whether Zejnil Delalic was commander or a member of the municipal staff of the TO Konjic?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, I was contacted by the Defence with these request and I responded to that request. In other words, I gave to the Defence what it asked for and what I had authority to give.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May the General now please be shown D144-5-A/27, page number 504. This is in Volume 2 of the military expert's report. May the English text also be placed on the ELMO. General, is this document-- did you or person authorised by you, issue it to the Defence on 22 May 1996?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, this is one of the documents which I issued, at the request of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since the witness confirmed that this is a document issued by the fourth corps command, at the request of the Defence, I offer it into evidence. Has it been accepted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: What do you want to do with it? He gave the certificate.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Ask him whether he gave the certificate.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I only asked that this certificate be added to the testimony as a corroboration of the testimony, and this would then conclude my questioning of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: All right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: (Microphone turned off) It's nice of you to admit it-- --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It's admitted. Let it come in. He's satisfied, because he's here in person. I don't know what is stronger than him being here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it was at least five times I was told that, in order to have it introduced, that I had to have it authenticated by the witness. I was following your instructions. And this happened at least five times before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I am satisfied it is saying the thing he certified. I don't think there's anything stronger than his being here in person.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. This concludes my examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Have we any cross-examination of the defence? Mr. Olujic, it is your witness now.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I, with your permission, I have very few questions. Cross-examined by Mr. Olujic

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, General.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am Zeljko Olujic, defence counsel for Mr. Zdravko Mucic. After the exhaustive examination of my learned colleague, I only have a couple of questions for you, a couple of comments that is. You are a professional officer who was trained in military academies. I believe that we will conclude this discussion very quickly. General, if I told you that in the former country, SFRY, and in the former Republic -- socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina the administration of prisons was entirely under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Justice, would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, I would agree with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. General, if I submitted to you that the former army did not have military prisons, but people were serving their sentences in regular prisons which were under the authority of the Ministry of Justice, would you also agree with me on that; in other words, that it only had detention facilities where people were staying for infractions which carried a sentence of up to 30 days. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: General, I have no further questions. Thank you very much. Your Honours, this concludes my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed, please, Mr. Karabdic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: Thank you. With your permission, I will ask a couple of questions. Cross-examined by Mr. Karabdic

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, a moment ago, when asked by my learned colleague, Ms. Residovic, you said that as commander of the Tactical Group you did not have the authority to appoint your own chief of staff or other members of your command. Was that your testimony, sir?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, I said that I did not appoint, nor did I have authority to appoint either the chief of staff or any other member of command of the Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this concern you only as a commander of the Tactical Group or was this a General rule? In other words, was it a rule that commanders at any level could not appoint either his chief of staff or other members of the command, but rather that these should be appointed by the same body which had appointed the commander himself?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: In the law on defence, and in the service in the armed forces, this has been regulated, that is those issues have been regulated, and it is clear at which level of command appointments are made, so which commanders or which commanding officers can appoint other commanding officers in other units. And, as a rule, commander of the units cannot appoint subordinate commanders within its own unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the rules it also -- the rules also stipulate that the commander cannot appoint his own deputy?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Further on you answered, when asked by my learned colleague, that as commander of the Tactical Group you did not have the right to punish your -- of your subordinates, that is, the other persons who were under your command in the Tactical Group. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: If I did not, I will state it now. I did not have the right to punish, because this was a temporary formation which was put together only to carry out certain combat tasks. If somebody did violate any rules, I would compile a report on it and send it to his home unit, and this unit was then in charge of prosecuting him, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly, that this rule only applies to Tactical Groups, because they are temporary formations?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. It is only for the Tactical Groups, because it is a temporary formation. Otherwise, other commanders of other units do have authority to punish their own subordinates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who has the right to punish?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: The exclusive right to punish lies with commanders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do the members of staff or their deputies have the right to punish?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: No, they do not have the right, unless they were authorised to do so specially. In other words, if they were given specific authority in that regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This concludes my cross-examination. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLER
utterances.text: (Microphone not on) Your Honours, there will be no cross-examination for the Defence of Esad Landzo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. From the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Yes, there will be cross-examination from the Prosecution. Thank you. Cross-examined by Ms. McHenry

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. My name is Teresa McHenry, and I am going to ask you some questions. If you don't understand a question, please tell me. I am also going to ask a number of questions that only require a "yes" or "no" answer, and where you can fairly do so, in order that we can move quickly, I ask that you just answer "yes" or "no". Okay?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Good morning. And, yes, if everything is clear. If it is not clear, then, unfortunately, we won't be able to do it that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fair enough. Now, sir, you indicated that when the war started your first task was to organise and lead the TO in Kiseljak, Busovaca, Kresevo and Fojnica. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you a member of the supreme command at that time?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was your title, your position as the organiser and leader of the TO?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Commander of the TO in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many municipalities does that encompass?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Four municipalities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, your appointment as commander of Tactical Group 1, was that in writing or done orally?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: I first received the oral appointment, and there is also an order in the supreme command staff with respect to this appointment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you receive your oral appointment, and when was the written appointment made?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Orally, I was informed of 12 May, and I believe that the order was also written down at that time, but, to be honest with you, I never saw it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And when you were given this assignment orally, were you told what your geographic zone of operation was?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: I did not have a geographic zone of responsibility, nor any other territorial zone. I pointed out that I had a direction through which I was supposed to try to lift the siege of Sarajevo, together with all the others who were engaged in that effort.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you told the direction, what would your zone of operation be?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you stated that you had seven positions on your staff, and that Mr. Delalic had those same seven positions when he became commander of Tactical Group 1. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: I believe that it was the same staff of the Tactical Group, because I know -- from what I recall, there was no change indicated on the part of the supreme command staff regarding the Tactical Group staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you indicated that you, in addition to Mr. Pilica and Mr. -- the deputy commander of logistics, Mr. Gagula, who were the other members of your staff?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: You mean by names?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, sir. All the ones you can remember.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: I will try to come up with some names and last names. Muhamed Turcinovic was the intelligence officer. The operations, that position changed several times. First it was Rekic, and I cannot recall the name of the other one. Amir was the chief of the cabinet, Kazazic was the communications person, and Kiba was a typist, and we mentioned Pilica and Gagula.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, who was your security officer?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: There was no security officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if that was -- well, let me tell you what was told yesterday, and then you tell me what part is incorrect. Yesterday you indicated that, "While the Tactical Group command was small, while I was on that duty, it had seven members, commander, chief of staff, operations or executive officer, logistics officer, security officer, chief officer, communications person, and the typist." Was that incorrect then? Was there a mistake?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Not security, but intelligence officer. It may have been a mistake in interpretation. There was never a security officer on the staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you mentioned the typist, the member of the command who served as your typist was Kiba. Do you know the full name of that person?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Kiba. It's a female name. I do not know her last name. I can't recall it now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, sir, you described the four stage manner in which you would get troops when you were Tactical Group commander, and I am not going to ask you to go over it all again, but part of the process involved you communicating with the supreme command in Sarajevo, and then the supreme command ordering the TO's to provide certain units. And my question is: Who in the supreme command did you communicate with?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: For the most part, with the chief of staff, Mr. Sefer Halilovic. In his absence, with the person who substituted for him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: We will now arise and we'll assemble at noon. --- Proceedings recessed at 11.30 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I remind you, sir, that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You may proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you indicated we had been talking about who in the supreme command you dealt with besides Mr. Halilovic, and you indicated that at some point, the forward command post at Visoko had certain authorisations over Tactical Groups, did I understand that correctly?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes. Those are authorisation given to that part of the command by the supreme command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly my question. What was the extent of the authorisation given to the Visoko forward command? What were they permitted to do in terms of the Tactical Groups?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: It concerns the authorisations of the forward command post. It referred to giving expert help in planning and preparation of combat activities. And to provide logistical support. These were the two basic functions concerning the authority of the forward command post in relation to the Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Tactical Group -- I'm sorry, did the Visoko forward command post have authority to issue orders to the Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, it did, but it happened only occasionally. Only in cases of the loss of communication with the supreme staff in, supreme command staff in Sarajevo, only in those staffs would they have the similar authority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, if I understand it, there was sort of a blanket authorisation that when the Tactical Group commanders could not get in touch with Sarajevo, they could just contact Visoko, and Visoko could then issue orders or authorise certain things? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, it is. But I repeat, it happened seldom that we would lose all communication links.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, let me ask that you be shown Defence Exhibit 183-1. And we can have the English put on the ELMO. It's the hand-written document from Mr. Delic. Sir, so was this a document that was issued during a time when you could not get in contact with Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: I have already said previously that the forward command post did have certain authorisations given to them by the chief of staff of the supreme command. Amongst those were certain authorisations to appoint certain commanders, certain officers to particular duties on the basis of which this appointment order was issued.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, let me see if I now understand you correctly, sir. Are you stating that even when you could get in touch with Sarajevo, the Visoko command post had authority to do certain things including issuing appointments?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see the actual authorisation given to the Visoko forward command post? Let me go back. Was it a written authorisation to the Visoko command post?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes. It existed and I also saw that order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And so it said, am I correct that it said it could provide help. It could provide logistic support and it said it could appoint persons to positions within the Tactical Group, is that correct? I am not sure, I heard you say "yes" in Serbo- Croat, but I did not hear it in English. Could the English interpretation booth tell us if they can communicate with us?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We hear you, but I don't think the witness said anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: The witness nodded his head. Just don't nod your head, say yes or no or any other answer you wish to give.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your prior answer to my question a "yes", sir?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: The answer to the previous question was "yes".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in addition to those things, was there any other authorisation given to the Visoko command post?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, depending on the assessment of the main staff of the supreme command in Sarajevo to perform tasks more efficiently, with more speed and then they would authorise for the enhancement or to make the defence system more efficient.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, basically it was a fluid situation and in situations where it was more efficient to have Visoko handle a matter, they were authorised to do so? Is that now a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I wish to be put in the transcript that this document was issued by Rasim Delic so that we avoid any possible confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: What was the confusion you had in mind? What confusion did you think could have caused? All that was being argued was whether a commander of a group could issue...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: The transcript states that the order was issued by Mr. Delic and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Not your client.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: I would like it to say Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He's saying that the transcript appears to attribute that letter to the accused, Hazim Delic, but the signature was Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Yes, and I think the document is part of the record, so I don't think there will be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Better correct it, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, would you like me to repeat my question? Am I correct now that there was, in effect, a fluid situation, so that in circumstances where it was more convenient or efficient for Visoko to handle a matter, they were authorised to do so?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Forward command post of Visoko has been established for those very needs. That is, to issue direct orders or to command directly to the entire defence system and the TO for the reason of the main staff being unable to be present in the field. They could not take the lead and the command directly over the units, so the purpose of the command post was such. That was the basic reason for its establishment. And, in addition to that, we mentioned some authorisations given to the forward command post to resolve certain problems in a more efficient manner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just to make sure I understand you, when you say they could not take the lead in the command directly over the units. So the purpose of the command post was such, you're referring to the Sarajevo headquarters could not take the lead and command directly over the units? Am I correct that's who you mean when they you say "they"? You have to say yes, sir, instead of nodding your head.--

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, I meant the main staff of the supreme command that is a part of the staff that was in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was Rasim Delic in the Visoko command post?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Was that the question, "When he was there"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Between April 13th or from the April 13th, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Until when?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Until when?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: A command post in Visoko was operational until May 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there other people besides Mr. Rasim Delic in the Visoko command post who were authorised to issue orders or appointments for the Tactical Groups?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Rasim Delic was the top person and the commander of the forward command post. Of course, he had his team of officers who would help him in his work and they had their own duties and authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me then ask you what I believe you have been given Document 183. Now, I note that the document refers to the Tactical Group 1 of Hadzici in that the seal apparently is the seal from the TO headquarters of the Visoko region. Now I assume those are just mistakes, am I correct on those?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: It is not clear to me. Do you mean this document that I have here?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I note that it refers to the TG-1 of Hadzici and if I understood you correctly yesterday, that, in fact, is a mistake, it's not the TG-1 of Hadzici, it's just the TG-1, correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: No, the mistake was not in that, but the mistake was that I mentioned was that the document stated, "Tactical Group 1, Konjic". So the mistake being the word "Konjic. "

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, is Tactical Group 1 of Hadzici, is that a correct or an incorrect term for the Tactical Group at that time?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: It is incorrect. We should always use the term Tactical Group 1 without any additions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I am not going to ask you about the seal, because I don't think it that's important. But let me ask you about another issue. Now this document is undated, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Which document?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The document in front of you, Document 183-1? Is there a date in the Bosnian version?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: There's no date here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see this document in 1992 soon after it was issued?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: I do not remember. I can't say for sure, it may have been possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, I assume you would agree with me that not having a date is a serious problem in knowing when persons were appointed and some might say that it makes this invalid. My question really is, is there a correction made to this document? Was there another document made to correct the mistakes in this one?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: I believe it was done, but I know for certain that both these commanders were in the part of the command from that day on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say from that date on, what date are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: The 12th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say you believe it was done, do you mean you believe that there was another appointment order made which corrected the serious problems?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next question, the next witness is Mr. Sucro, so I don't think the appropriate questions were being asked of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Since it was Ms. Residovic who showed him the document and it does refer to his Tactical Group, I thought it was fair to ask him, obviously, if he doesn't know, he can simply say, "I don't know. "

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He doesn't even remember saying this. He didn't remember seeing it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I correct, sir, that you don't know if there was another made until after this one, which may have corrected it or altered it in any way?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: The only issue at stake here is the issue of the date, nothing else needed correction. I claim that Mustafa Gagula and Sucro Pilica were members of the command from there on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He can tell you the date of his appointment.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I'll move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you stated that there were rules saying at what level commanders could appoint their own staff, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Not his own people, the commander could never appoint his own staff. It could only be done by a superior command or commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that true for all levels of staff? In other words, no matter how minor the appointment of the staff member was, a commander did not have authority to appoint someone to that position?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: No, the commander could never appoint his immediate subordinates. This is always done by the next superior command. For example, a troop, the appointments can be made at the lowest level by the commander of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, now, are you saying that there are rules or regulations in the Bosnian army that provide for this?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, they have existed and they are still in existence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now let me ask that you be shown Prosecution Exhibit 230, which is ... And I'll ask that the English be put on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a document from the archives. Now, sir, if I understand you correctly, Mr. Delalic had no authority to make this appointment. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Such appointments commander can issue only temporarily, until they get the final appointment from the -- from a superior command, in case of an emergency that required a reappointment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, the commander did have authority to appoint his staff on a temporary basis. Is that correct now?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: If this was required by the emergent nature of the situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that in the regulations too, that if it's an emergency, the commander can do it himself?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, it is regulated by directions and authorities of all commanders at command posts. These are just exceptional cases when this needs to be done because of the current tasks and the needs of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that in General, the military rules and regulations are set up to be flexible, and so that when there is a pressing need or emergency, exceptions can be made?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Apologies. We heard "January" in the interpretation, and I don't think that it appeared. And if I do not understand it, I don't see how the witness could understand it properly.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Let me repeat the sentence, since I certainly did not say "January".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, would you agree with me that in General, not in January, the military rules and regulations were set up to be flexible and allow for exceptions where there was a need?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: The specific nature of the military organisation and operation consists also in -- that in a particular situation such clauses also have to be introduced, and this refers especially to, let's say, a situation of war and combat operation. For instance, if the commander is killed, we know that if you wait for an order of this superior command to issue an order appointing a new commander, this is a very long road. I gave you an example that is pretty drastic, but you use a speedier way. So a commander may be given authority to appoint another commander until a proper order is issued later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, sir, let me go on then to another subject. Actually, let me just -- speaking of what we were just talking about. You earlier described, and again I am not going to ask you to describe it again, the rather cumbersome procedure by which, when you were head of the Tactical Group, you would get soldiers, which required you reconnaissance, talking to supreme command, the supreme command issuing orders, the TO command issuing orders, et cetera. Now, the cumbersome nature of this procedure, is this why, when the JUG group was created, the JUG group was given the authorisation to itself determine what TO troops would participate in JUG actions?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: As far as the activities of the JUG group are concerned, I am not that familiar with them. As far as I know, a separate command was established there into which Tactical Groups, but also other units, belonged. So this is why a separate command was established for this task, and it existed only as long as the task was still on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what Tactical Groups were part of JUG, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: As far as I know, the Tactical Group 1, groups 1 and 2, took part in this operation, that is in that main area or direction. At the same time the Tactical Group Visoko was also involved in these operations, but they were not under the command of the group JUG.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was Tactical Group 2 created, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: I said that yesterday. This was on 15 June or in the middle of the month. I believe -- I think it was around the 15th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was before your accident; is that correct? It was while -- it was while you were still commander of Tactical Group 1; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, this was while I was still commander of the Tactical Group 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: There is confusion again. There are two dates, of 15 June and 15 July, for the exact same fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: But he used both months, June, July. First he said 15 June, then he said around about the next -- he said 15 July. He has corrected himself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I correct that it was 15th of July that you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, 15th of July, or the seventh month, if you will.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, sir, you testified about when you received certain -- may I have the help of the usher. When you received certain troops from Konjic. I am going to show you a document, and there are extra copies for Counsel and the Judges.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution document 249.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, let me ask you, did you see this document in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: I saw this document in June of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I note that the beginning of this document says, "In order to support the units active in Hadzici area, pursuant to an order from republican headquarters, I hereby order." Now, sir, you would agree with me that it was normal for a commander to pass onto his subordinates and to implement the orders that the commander received from his higher command?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, this is the regular procedure. In other words, the commander of the municipal staff received an order from the republican staff to set aside certain personnel, and he specifically is issuing the order as to which personnel who is commanding officer there, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I think it's clear, isn't it, that the fact that it says, "pursuant to an order from republican headquarters," doesn't mean that Mr. Ramic had no authority over the TO troops under his command?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: I don't know what you want to say by that. Mr. Ramic has complete authority to command of the republican staff of Konjic. Here you can say that he received an order from the republican staff to set aside some personnel for the Tactical Group 1, that is, for the area or the direction of operation, and I see it as perfectly clear. I hope you do too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was normal -- it was not unusual, when a commander was passing along orders to his own subordinates, for the commander to indicate that he had received an order from his higher command? That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I notice --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. If I may interrupt for a second. Pursuant to Rule 66 of the Rules, Prosecution has an obligation to provide all the documents to the Defence. I must point out that the Defence never received this document from the Prosecution, and that the Prosecution is directly in violation of this Rule.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: If I may respond. This is a document we received from Ms. Residovic herself on the 4th of July, 1996. It may be that Ms. Residovic has forgotten that fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I notice that this document has two seals and one signature. When you saw it in 1992, did it also have two seals and one signature?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: I believe that it did, but here it states clearly who the commander is and who has the right to issue orders --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I don't think there is a question, so it may be -- I haven't asked a question yet.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Very well. I will wait.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it usual or unusual for you to see documents in 1992 that had seals on them without a signature? Let me ask it another way. What's the purpose of a seal on a document?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: It is usual with -- in our own practice, and this is still in force today, that the seals are affixed to the documents, and this is actually to prove in which institution, which unit, which command, a certain document was compiled, and where it is being kept. And a person who are signatories are the ones who stand behind them, that is, in this particular case, behind this order. And this is still in effect with us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Just a minute. As far as I can see, these seem to be similar seals, two impressions of the same seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I am happy to ask the witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He's got probably the original.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, are you able to tell whether or not these seals come from the same body or not?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: You cannot see clearly, but it is possible they are from the same institution. Again, let me point out that this is to trace the institution in which this document was registered and in which it was drafted. And if a document was compiled, let's say in the staff of the municipal headquarters of the TO Konjic, then it bears the stamp of this Konjic TO staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, since the witness has indicated that this is a true and accurate copy of a document he received a copy of in 1992, I ask that it be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, it's admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I am correct, aren't I, that the Gajret unit which is referred to here did not actually join Tactical Group --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Just a minute. Just I was wondering -- just a minute, please. The --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour. To Judge Jan, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: (No microphone) One of the signatories, although he has not signed it, is probably the coordinator. Why send a then to the coordinator? If he's also one of the originators of the document, why send a copy to him?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Possibly for his own --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You want this document to be put on the record, admitted into evidence. I just want to find out, because it is now your document, can you explain that to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can certainly explain a number of reasons why it might happen, including that the coordinator would want to make sure that he had a copy for his own files.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: But he's the originator of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Why his name appears in the list of those copied, that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: That is your document. I just wanted to find out.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can give you why I presume it's the case, but I can't give evidence, so I'm not sure you will be satisfied --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
