utterances.text: Surely, you must have looked at the document and you must have seen that. You must have sought information.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm not going to give evidence, but I think it's rational to assume that the coordinator, given that another copy goes to files, it could be that in addition to the files of the TO and HVO headquarters, the coordinator wanted his own file. But, Your Honour, I'm not -- I certainly am not going to be able to explain every single document that comes into evidence. And that's in fact one of the reasons why we show these documents, is to show that there was some confusion and some lack of clarity about exactly what was going on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: It is your document. You should be able to tell us. The explanation has to come from you, because you are relying upon this document, telling us that it's a reliable document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Explain to us this little, seemingly, discrepancy.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've given you one, what I think, plausible explanation. The witness has said that this is a reliable document, but with respect to every nuance, I don't think it's going to be the case that we can in every single instance explain every discrepancy, because this was a wartime situation. And I think the way things were working was not always in accordance with sort of strict lines of procedure, or always even one hundred percent rational.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, you will -- the Rule on this, however, I would just like to state for the transcript that this document has no reference with respect to Zejnil Delalic, and we have heard about a whole range of persons who were coordinators during that period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: It refers to a coordinator, not necessarily your client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: A general provision.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Let me go on, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am correct, aren't I, that the Gajret unit, which is actually referred to in this document, did not actually join Tactical Group 1 until at least the 20th of June. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: That is not correct, as far as the date is concerned, because we have already stated that this unit joined on the 12th rather than 20th of June. It is correct that it did join the Tactical Group, or was subordinated to the Tactical Group, but it was the 12th June until 18 of June when these combat operations which had been planned for it were completed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you are sure about those dates? Is that what I am understanding you --

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Completely certain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, you indicated that some of the TO units who provided units had district headquarters that were operating, such as Zenica. Did I understand, or it's my assumption from what you stated yesterday, that the district staff was not involved in this process by which the Tactical Groups would communicate with the supreme command, and the supreme command would communicate with the districts -- with the TO headquarters? Is it correct that the district staff did not play any role in this operation that you've described?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Apologies. There may be a problem in interpretation, but I understood -- I could not understand -- I did not understand the way the question was phrased. So for those of us who are unable to follow it in the original, can it please be restated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, did you understand the question? Would you like me to repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: It is a rather comprehensive question. Maybe I can answer it part by part, or else I can offer an equally comprehensive answer. I cannot answer your question with a simple "yes" or "no" or with just a couple of words.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's fair enough, sir. And let me just, to make sure that Ms. Residovic understands, the question was whether or not in this operation by which the Tactical Groups would get troops by communicating with the supreme command and the supreme command communicating with the TO units. Did the district staffs that were operating play any role? And, sir, please explain.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, they did play a role. The district staffs were also involved, that is the ones that were operational at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you explain in this operation that you've discussed, where you would communicate with the supreme command and then the supreme command would communicate with the TO headquarters, where is it in this process that the district staff played a role?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: The transmission of orders to the municipal staffs who were under their authorities. For example, in the specific case we can give a good illustration on the municipal staff of Prozor, which was under the command of the district command in Zenica, and it was through them that they received orders to set aside certain troops for the Tactical Groups.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I would ask that you be shown the chart again, the one that you compiled, D145/6/3. It's pages 893 and 894. I believe it's in Volume 3. Now, sir, this chart is dated from May to November, and indicates that during the JUG operation, in addition to the troops shown on the chart, there were an additional 200 troops attached to Tactical Group 1. Is that correct? And I think that's actually not shown on the ELMO. I think it's a little below that.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: It's one of the General charts which is shown in order to better understand how the Tactical Groups worked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: It does not refer -- I mean, that is the correct part of it, but the relations that we talked about a moment ago are not represented here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir, I don't understand. What relations do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: You asked me how the municipal staff received orders, whether the district staffs had played a role in it, and I said that they did, and I gave you this example.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I understand that, and I understand that that is not represented on the chart and my questions are not related to that. These are new questions about a different subject matter. And my particular question is: Am I correct that in addition to the chart -- to the troops that were shown in the actual chart itself as being part of Tactical Group 1 during the JUG operation, Tactical Group 1 had an additional 200 troops? And I am specifically making -- just basing that question on remark 2.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: I said a Tactical Group or the troops of the Tactical Group were of a temporary formation, and the forces are not the same for two operations, and they may not be the same regarding the force, the type of personnel, et cetera. So I am giving -- this is just a General way in which certain units were set aside in order to assemble a particular unit for a particular task. And it does not mean that it was factually so. So this is not a formation that was used for the JUG operation, nor is it a formation for any specific operation. This is just to generally show how this came about, how this was done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, then, let me clarify, sir. Is this chart, including the remarks that are made part of it, an accurate depiction of the composition of Tactical Group 1 from May to November of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: It cannot be a representation of the accurate composition of the Tactical Group, because the forces within the Tactical Groups change. There were periods when you had just the command staff and maybe up to 100 personnel, or troops, so this was not a composition that was there throughout this period. It was always only done in order to carry out certain operation, and at the end of it these troops are then returned to their home bases, to their units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you actually draw up this chart?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, we did put it together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "we", who else besides you compiled this chart?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: We did this in the fourth corps command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So who else, besides you, participated in creating this chart?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: My staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who is the member of your staff, sir? Who participated in making this chart?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You mean by who helped duties, who gave information?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: How many other people were there who helped you make up this chart?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He's signed as a person who produced it. I think if you have any questions, ask him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then, sir, let me ask you what is meant by remark 2 when it says, "To strengthen Tactical Group 1 for JUG operations, it had additional 200 soldiers?"

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: This was an example which says that this composition of Tactical Group was changed. It can be changed at any time, depending on the available force, and the Tactical Group can be larger or smaller.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think the Trial Chamber will now rise and we'll reassemble at 2.30. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.02 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I remind you, sir, that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Ms. McHenry.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, before lunch we had talked about who had authority to appoint command staff. I just want to make sure I understood you correctly, unless it was an emergency, the head of the Territorial Defence had no authority to appoint the persons who would be part of his staff within the Territorial Defence? Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: He could only do what was allowed for him to do under the law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did the law provide with respect to Territorial Defence commanders appointing their own staff?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: He could not appoint his staff, but he could appoint staff to his subordinate units. And when I say "units", it means officers, together with squad leaders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Now, it's correct, sir, that when you were a commander of Tactical Group 1, there were sometimes MUP units that were made part of your Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, there were such instances.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how about troops from other entities, such as HOS units, did you have any other such units when you were commander of Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: When I was commander, we had no people from such units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that when Mr. Delalic was commander of Tactical Group 1 he did have HOS units under him?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: I am not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you would agree with me that in cases where MUP units or whatever other units were part of a Tactical Group, they then were under the higher authority of the supreme command? For the period that they were part of the Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: No, if they were given to a Tactical Group during that period of time they were under the command of the commander of the Tactical Group, as well as all the other formations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, sir, am I correct, aren't I, that the higher authority to the Tactical Group was a supreme command?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes. A main staff of the supreme command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, and so wouldn't that mean that the MUP units that were part of the Tactical Group were under the, for that period of time, under the authority also of the supreme command?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Only during the combat activity, yes, within that period. This would follow from the authorities of the Tactical Group for that period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, sir, you talked about that tactical groups had important, urgent needs for intelligence, information and logistical support and you indicated that tactical groups could ask for assistance in those regards from Territorial Defence headquarters, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you would agree with me that Tactical Groups had authority to issue orders to TO commanders about intelligence matters?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, but only under the authorities given to them or orders given to them by the supreme command. This includes the providing of intelligence data, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how about logistical support?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Concerning logistic support, they could deal with requests for equipping the troops and units that a particular municipal staff or TO headquarters sets aside for the use of the Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, with respect to some of these matters, you mentioned a directive, now is a directive an order, a regulation or something else?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: The provision issued by the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and would be valid until another regulation or a provision referring to that particular issue would appear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do I understand you, sir, that you're stating that there was a specific regulation which dealt with the issue of tactical -- I mean, that dealt with the issue of Territorial Defence headquarters, providing intelligence matters to tactical groups?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: No, this is not regulated in that manner, this is regulated by an order of the superior command to meet those requirements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you yourself see this order? Was it in written form? Let me ask you that first. Was it in written form?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, it was in a written form. I personally did not see it, but it is part of the files. I know that such orders were transmitted to communication links and that they would receive such orders in full certainty in that manner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just ask that you be shown Prosecution Exhibit 224. It was shown to you during direct. Let me also just notify the registrar that the next document that I ask that he be shown is D-146. It was also shown to him during direct. Now, sir, you would agree with me that nowhere in this order from Mr. Delalic to Konjic headquarters about intelligence is there any mention of any kind of directive or order from the supreme command?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, there's no mention of it here concerning the order of the supreme command staff, but my previous statement, I mentioned that in such cases, in addition to an order like this one, it should have been appended with a directive from the main staff of the supreme command to make this order valid and binding for municipal staffs. Unless, it is not there, this order would not be binding for municipal staffs because municipal staffs are not under the command of the commander of a Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let me follow up. Well, certainly in cases where there's an attachment that forms an integral part of a document, that is usually reflected in the document itself?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Together with the document, it should also have with it an original copy as an annex to it coming from the supreme command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you stated, again referring to this document that Mr. Delalic had no authorisation to ensure that this order was carried out. The last sentence which states; "that the commander of the TO is responsible to me for compliance with this order," what does that mean to you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Only in the case of such obligations tied to specific activities. In this case it is reconnaissance and intelligence gathering, due to the emergency and the need for obtaining such information. The commander warns the TO commanders of their responsibility. If those informations are not admitted in time, they will be held responsible if the Tactical Group is incapable of performing the task. I personally think this was a mistake. This should not have been formulated in this way in a text that they are responsible to him. They are responsible to the supreme command if they do not abide.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you were a commander of Tactical Group 1, were you considered part of the supreme command?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: No, I have not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you issue written orders when you were commander of Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, but only to my units whilst they were a part of the TG.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you did not issue any written orders about intelligence matters or similar items, did you?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: No, there was no need for me to do that. When I was commander, there was no such problems. There was absolutely no need for this. I believe Delalic did this because he must have been at a situation where that was needed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me refer you to the heading of this document in front of you, where it says, "Headquarters of the Supreme Command of the Armed Forces, Sarajevo, Tactical Group 1," when you issued written orders, when you were commander of the Tactical Group, did you use that same heading?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you would agree with me that this heading would indicate that Tactical Groups are considered part of the supreme command?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: No, they are subordinate to the supreme command. This points out that TGs are supreme commands subordinate to units. At least in the army it has been structured that way, to see the superior command and then the command that issues a given document or order or a directive and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, under that reasoning, when TO headquarters issued orders, they would also have headquarters of the supreme command of the armed forces and then they would have TO headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, it would.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, previously you mentioned that Visoko command post and also the Visoko Tactical Group, what relationship, if any, was there between these two entities?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: There was communication, forward command post was a part of the supreme command, which was outside of Sarajevo. And all the TGs, including TG-1, and Tactical Group Visoko, was subordinated to the supreme command and this then applies to the forward command post as well. Tactical Group Visoko is subordinate to the supreme command as well as all the other formations in the area of the Republic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, with respect to the 27th of July order regarding Mr. Delalic, where he's given certain authority, you stated that this document took a long time to arrive, that you heard about it orally and it took a long time to arrive, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I correct then that you did not even see that order before you had your accident in August?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, I would say so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after your accident in August, am I correct that you were out for approximately six months?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: That's what he said yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Did he say six months, I'm sorry, I didn't remember it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would ask that the witness now be shown D-146-1. Again, this is a document that you saw in direct. Now, sir, in direct examination you gave your opinion about this document and I would just like to clarify that your opinions about the document are speculation in that you didn't see this document in 1992 and you didn't talk to anybody about why it was issued, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: That was my comment as a professional soldier, why there was a necessity for this document because a previous document was very unclear, too generalised, and the military practice, such documents are not considered reliable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just remind you, just if you can, just listen to my question. My question wasn't for you to explain your opinion again. My question was to clarify that you didn't see this document in 1992 and you didn't talk to anybody about why it was created in 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Is that why he cannot express an opinion?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I haven't said he can't express an opinion, I am just clarifying the basis for that opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It's in the document, and he's compared it with practice and he can tell you what he thinks the content of the document. That's what he was saying. Not anything -- I think he just tells you what he feels that document represents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's correct, sir, that your opinion about what this document represents doesn't mean that you saw this document in 1992 or know why it was -- why this document was created as a matter of fact?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: I have said that I did not see the document, I just commented on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Now, you would agree with me, sir, that often President Izetbegovic affirmed the appointments that had already been made for purposes, including for publication in the official gazette?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Not only published. I have mentioned that in the emergency situations, commanders who did not have the authority under the law would still appoint commanders to certain posts or give certain duties. For all the persons that the presidency had authority over, then additionally they had to verify those temporary orders made in such instances. That was their authority, their duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, let me ask that you look at this document closely, sir. And in it, there's an indication that the documents are based on a proposal by the Minister of Defence of 19th of July, 1992. Now would you agree with me, wouldn't you, that it wouldn't make sense for this order to have been made to clarify an on order that hadn't even been made on July 19th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: He could see when the document was drafted. This is just a link from the Ministry of Defence, it does not have to refer to everything in the document because they mentioned several provisions and regulations in the law, including the position, the recommendation of the Minister of Defence. This does not means it refers directly to what I commented on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you, sir, with respect to that same document, this description of the area of Tactical Group 1, Hadzici, Pazaric, Konjic and Jablanica, is that an accurate description of the zone of operations of Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Looking at the description of the area, they were not, the facilities and the names are not put in line looking at it geographically, otherwise it should be fine. They are reversed in order. And we as soldiers usually go in the direction of the enemy, but these names are valid and this is the direction, this is the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, at this time, Tactical Group was operational in those four municipalities, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Tactical Group was there only to attempt to lift the siege off of Sarajevo. Stated here are the areas from which Tactical Group would take units to compose them -- to fulfil the number of needed soldiers for the operation i.e. The municipal staffs and the TO headquarters which were obliged to set aside a number of units for the needs of the Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, these four municipalities listed here do not indicate where Tactical Group 1 was actually operating, but they indicate the municipalities from which Tactical Group 1 had some units?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, the on the transcript we miss -- there's a word that is missing, which means mainly or usually. The latest quoting, "would take units" and the General said, "would usually take units."

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you understand my question or do I need to repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: If you could repeat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly, that these four municipalities listed here, that they do not represent the area of operations of Tactical Group 1, but instead represent the municipalities for which Tactical Group 1 usually took some units?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: How does a Tactical Group usually take -- when it is about ad hoc creation?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I believe I am using his own words, if it's not correct, I assume, he'll correct me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The type of question is misleading. It's not a standing order, it's about areas where they would usually take things.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My answer again is that these are the staffs, command staffs from these municipalities which had an obligation to allocate or set aside parts of their units for the Tactical Group 1. That is the point of this order, that this is a standing obligation. So not municipalities, but municipal staffs from that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it does not represent the area of operation of Tactical Group 1, correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: No. The area of operation of Tactical Group 1, as I pointed out yesterday, was Pazaric, Hadzici, Ilidza. That is where it was operating in terms of combat, but these are the areas from which the units are used for, set aside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, sir, you stated in direct -- I am finished with that document. Thank you. Sir, you stated that there was a rule that said Tactical Groups had no authority to discipline troops placed under their command; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: We did not have the authority over the troops as far as the penal provisions are concerned, those who were part of the Tactical Group 1 for this brief task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you state that there was a rule to this effect, a rule or a regulation, or order?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Just legal provisions which enumerated and stipulated exactly the duties, together with the rights, as well as the authority when the discipline was concerned. And in no such provision, order or directive, was the Tactical Group or the commander of Tactical Group given such an authority.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Just a minute. As I understand, in Pakistan, different types of court marshals dealing with different offences, like the field court marshall, the General court marshall, do you have the same thing in -- a special court marshall, do you have anything like that in the Bosnia Army?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Not now. Now it's unified orders. No special court marshall in our Army. All cases of Prosecution are taken over by the civilian courts and all these cases are then resolved in the civilian courts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: What was the position in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: In '92 there were some wartime court marshals which did handle these cases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Could a TG commander order a field court marshall or a general court marshall or a special court marshall?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: No. Commander of the Tactical Group only had a possibility to give information on the person who has violated the discipline and turned him over to his home-based unit, and then this unit would then go on and prosecute, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you would agree with me that there was nothing in writing anywhere which indicated -- which stated that Tactical Group commanders did not have authority to discipline the troops under their command?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: There was nothing in writing anywhere with respect to the commander of Tactical Group being able to discipline his troops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that it's an extraordinary departure from standard military practice that a commander, who has authority to issue orders to troops under his command, has no authority to discipline those troops?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Apparently, you do not appreciate how short a period of time is covered by these troops being part of the Tactical Groups. I gave you several examples of what periods of time these were. It never exceeded 10 days. So there was absolutely no need to give such an authority to the commander of a Tactical Group, because if in, let's say, in this first case we -- there was a period of 20 to 28th May and then 10 to 18 June and then 10 to 15 July, then you can see how long these troops stayed within their formation. And the Tactical Group commander doesn't have the time to deal with these things. That would be absurd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I think it was wrong. It's not a special but summary court marshall. Did you have the power to hold summary court marshals?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: No, we did not have such courts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This understanding of yours, that Tactical Group commanders did not have authority to discipline troops, were there exceptions to this, such as when the Tactical Group was in an area where it couldn't immediately send someone back to its parent unit?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: There were no such cases, at least while I was a commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Judge Jan asked you what happened with Tactical Group 1 prisoners, and you responded that Tactical Group 1 did not have prisons. Let me ask you this: During the entire course of operations of Tactical Group 1, was anyone ever captured or did anyone ever surrender?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: While I was the commander, no. And there are reasons for it. And, if necessary, I can also explain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you would agree with me that in 1992 there were no regulations concerning who ran military prisons?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Isn't it his evidence there were no military prisons?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I don't believe that he stated that, Your Honour. If so, he can tell me that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me clarify. Is it the case that in 1992, in all of Bosnia-Herzegovina there were no military prisons?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: As far as I know, there were none.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask that you be shown this chart with your signature verifying its accuracy. I have extra copies, and I ask that the English -- well, there's extra copies.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution document 250.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Can we have the English on the ELMO also, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, is this your signature on this chart?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, this is my signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does this chart accurately reflect your understanding of who had authority over the prison and the Celebici barracks by month?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: I really don't know who had authority. These data were taken from the agency which deals with prisons. These are not military prisons. This is General prison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I didn't ask if it was a military prison. I just asked whether or not, given that you have signed this, this document reflects your understanding of who had authority over the Celebici prison.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: As I said, this document was prepared by persons who must have had the appropriate data. I did sign this document, even though specifically regarding this authority I never verified it, nor did I have an opportunity to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, when it says "accuracy of verified by fourth corps commander, Brigadier Mustafa Polutak," what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: As I said, based -- on the basis of documents which were used to create this chart, this should be accurate, and that it should mean that I have verified it and that I signed it. However, I said that personally I did not verify it, but on the basis of the documents available, this was produced and I did sign it as such.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does this -- does the same hold true with the third chart on the same document, which states, "duties of Delalic"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I'm sure you can't even understand these documents. Do you understand this?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, for the most part, again according to the knowledge and data, the activities of Zejnil Delalic during this period, for the most part they were in logistics, then coordination between the war presidency of the Konjic municipality and the Konjic defence forces, and then as commander of Tactical Group 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Thank you. I would move into evidence Prosecution Exhibit 250.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Before you move further, I want to ask the General a question.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: In this chart, chart number 3, you described him to be a soldier. He is merely a civilian. Why did you describe him as a soldier?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: This is some kind of mistake. Not as a soldier. You are right, not as a soldier. Only as a logistics person. He only engaged in procurement or acquisition of logistical materiel for the military. So not a soldier, because at that time he was not a soldier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: What do the Roman figures --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Months.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: -- indicate?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Roman numerals designate months.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Now you can move to the other subject, as you say.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just actually ask you. Sir, you would agree with me that someone who has authority to engage in -- to enter into agreements about joint actions of troops has a military function, at least with respect to that?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Can you please repeat this?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, would you agree with me that someone who had authority to enter into agreements on joint actions of troops, that that would constitute a military function rather than a civilian function?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: As far as reaching agreements is concerned, this "constitute" is a bit vague in the military. Maybe it was something very -- for us maybe coordination was more appropriate. Where the HVO and the Territorial Defence acted on a parallel basis, and since they were not under a joint command, there was a need to coordinate between these two forces or these two formations. Here, Zejnil Delalic is not mentioned and, as far as I know, he was not a coordinator between the HVO and the Army, that is the TO, but between the war presidency and the defence forces in the Konjic area. So that would be the connection. That would be closer to what his role of coordinator was, even though part of his job may also have involved attempt to narrow the gap and bridge the differences between the HVO and the TO. But the actual military functions were performed by the commanders of the HVO and the TO. That is, that was all performed at a command for -- because for a while there was a joint command in Konjic between the HVO and the TO.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I have no additional questions for -- with respect to this exhibit, but I would ask that it be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, it's admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, sir, would you agree with me that it would not be possible for the legitimate government of Bosnia-Herzegovina to absolve itself of responsibility under the Geneva Conventions for POW's merely because there were no regulations governing military prisons?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: This is a legal question. How can he answer? You are asking about legal opinions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I am going to show you another chart, please, that you have drawn or, excuse me, that has your signature.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution document 251.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you would agree with me that this document also bears your signature?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, this is my signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, in fact, this document is similar to the document already admitted into evidence. But let me ask you, does this document accurately reflect your understanding that soldiers in the TO were directly subordinate to the main staff of the Army and partly subordinate to the war presidencies?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: You mean in the remark underneath? Is that what you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's correct. I am referring to the note, and I am asking whether or not that note, the chart, the whole document, accurately reflects your understanding that soldiers in the TO were directly subordinate to the main staff and partly subordinate to war presidencies?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: All units were subordinate to the main staff. I would just like to point out here that why it states that partly to the TO's -- it's the term municipal TO's. This is what it actually states. It's a very small number of troops and these are the units of -- for information, and they are with the staff, with municipal staffs, and they are directly controlled and commanded by the ministry, so this is a very small number of persons who are involved in the communications, people who are in charge of mobilisation, and so on. So these are -- this is a very small number of persons. We are talking about 10 to 15 people here with respect to the relation between the war presidency and these persons who are subordinate to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Just a minute. What do the letters "RPS" stand for? In the Bosnian version there is a description, not in the English translation. In the Bosnian version there is an extra translation of these two letters, but not in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: It's war presidency of these municipalities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: (Microphone not on) What does "RP" stand for?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Is it correct that the letter "RP" stands for war presidency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: (Microphone not on) War presidency is mentioned separately.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I think that's the notation of the translation section. They put something in brackets when it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Not a slash, but a bracket?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry, I didn't understand that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, sir, there were some number of soldiers, a small number of TO soldiers, who had partial subordination to the war presidency; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: These are not TO soldiers. These are soldiers or personnel from the ministry who are engaged in the matters concerning the information, alert, and similar activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there are some persons who are soldiers, who are fully subordinate to the main staff and partly subordinate to war presidencies; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, through the Ministry of Defence, the small number of people that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honours, I would ask that 251 also be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Actually, what is the purpose?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the purpose is it's a chart which explains his understanding of tactical and operative groups, including his understanding that there were soldiers in the municipality who were fully subordinate to the main staff, and partially subordinate to the war presidencies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: -- soldiers within the region, within the area?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I believe -- yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Okay. It's admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you stated that you met Mr. Delalic during the time that he was coordinator. Am I correct that one of the times you met Mr. Delalic was in mid-May 1992 in Dusina, when the first efforts to lift the siege of Sarajevo were being planned?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: It is correct that I met Mr. Delalic for the first time in Dusina, but not -- but at the time when we met, the lifting of the siege of Sarajevo was not being planned. It had been planned earlier. But I was in Dusina in order to find out how much of the materiel would be possible to set aside for the lifting of the siege, so that I can plan my combat activities. I can explain that too, why Dusina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am not going to ask you about that, sir. Sir, I am correct that Mr. Rasim Delic was in Dusina also?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in what capacity was Mr. Delic there?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: At that moment we were waiting for one of the larger convoys, which were meant to supply for the needs of the units. Amongst other authorities, Rasim Delic also had the duty to distribute those supplies. In that case we should decide on the distribution of that materiel and equipment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Does this evidence help you in any way?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I correct that you were there in your capacity as Tactical Group 1 commander?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, at that time I was a commander of Tactical Group 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in addition to meeting Mr. Delalic before he was Tactical Group commander, you met him after he left Bosnia, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, I met with him once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And am I correct that you got in contact with Mr. Delalic after he left Bosnia to help with the war effort, and later you went to Vienna to attend a meeting of the Bosnian association headed by Mr. Delalic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: It is not true. I did speak -- I did not speak with Delalic, I spoke with our association in Vienna about that meeting. To be more precise, all the arrangements were done through Mr. Velagic and the representative of the SDA party, who was in Vienna, together with his associates, meaning the BiH association, and upon my arrival to Vienna, amongst other people, I met also with Mr. Delalic, because he would also come around to that association, and that's where I met him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you would agree with me that you, during one of these occasions, there is in fact a video in which you stated that you got in touch with Mr. Delalic, and Mr. Delalic accepted to be president of the steering committee to connect the people of Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Velagic was the main person for the arrangement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if there is a videotape showing you saying this, would you say that it's not correct, or do you just say that you don't remember?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: I would say it is incorrect, because a direct agreement, a direct communication with Delalic I did not have. The main organiser of the meeting was Teofik Velagic. His people would come to Jablanica to see Savko Bitanga, and I can't remember the other persons names, so that's how we communicated through those people about our coming to Vienna, not with Zejnil Delalic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honours, the name has been misspelled. Once it is Velagic and the next time it was Velagic. The correct name is Teofik Velagic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, let me move on to something else. You stated that in addition to the main combat task of a Tactical Group commander, the supreme command could give tactical groups additional tasks, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, I have said that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when was your accident in August, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: August 25th, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you would agree with me that after your accident in August, you don't know what tasks were given Mr. Delalic by the supreme command?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: If he received special tasks after 25th, then I wouldn't know that for certain and I presume there was no such case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And let's talk about the period before the 25th, did you know every task given to Mr. Delalic by the supreme command?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: No, not every task specifically. But when we speak about authorities, I am certain that they were not changed until the 25th, the ones relating to the commander of the TG.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you, sir, you would agree with me and indeed I have believed you stated previously when asked about Mr. Delalic's responsibilities as Tactical Group 1 commander, "I cannot say whether his responsibilities as commander of the Tactical Group had been increased compared with the time when I was commander of Tactical Group 1." Is that a correct statement, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I am not sure he has said anything differently.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe I have said that he did not receive greater authority, but the area of activity was reduced because at that time we had the Tactical Group 2 established. That was my comment. His authorities were not greater, expanded, only the area was reduced.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, let me just ask you, isn't it correct that previously, when asked about Mr. Delalic's responsibilities, you said, "I cannot say whether his responsibilities as commander of the Tactical Group had been increased compared with the time when I was commander of Tactical Group 1." Did you say that previously?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Even if he did and it was different, you must have been wrong, that's all. Why all that?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He can't be wrong, he's not the one doing it. Someone else is giving the authority.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: But he said "da." You said "yes"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I answered "yes".

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Thank you. We have no further questions, thank you. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You have any re-examination, you can. Thank you very much. Re-examined by Ms. Residovic

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, during cross-examination, you spoke of the authorities of the commander of the Tactical Group or another commander concerning appointments stemming from his authorities. You were also shown appointment document about the appointment of Mr. Pilica Sukro. Did the command superior to commander of the Tactical Group could give authorities to him, authorities that would refer to appointing of certain people?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: In correspondence to their authorities, superior command can give their subordinate commanders certain authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Such an authority, would it be in compliance with the military science?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, it would.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you were also shown the structure of the Tactical Group put together by you, you said before the Chamber precisely that we have an organisational chart which need not be put into reality at any given moment. The chart that was signed by you, would it represent a planned or possible number of soldiers that the particular Tactical Group would need or is it a fixed number of soldiers belonging to the Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: This is a planned figure. Planned forces. I have said earlier that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: (Microphone not on) -- for you to explain. It wasn't ambiguous. It was very clear. It shows the strength of the formations at that time and those who contributed and how many people they contributed. There's nothing ambiguous about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is the controversy because the witness responding to the Prosecution's answers -- questions, gave certain answers that I wanted clarified. He confirmed now that these numbers, planned number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The question you should re-examine about must be arising from what cross-examination had introduced. That is all you are entitled to do. Where there's no ambiguity in what the cross-examination raised throughout.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, when we speak of the shown document dated June 11 on the establishing of Gajret, did the municipal staff, which has command over all the units in its territory authorised to subordinate those units without a command from a -- without an order from a supreme command to give, to set aside for some other command?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: I think I understood. Without a supreme command's order, municipal staff could not subordinate its units to any other commander. It must have been an order existent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the last question, engagement of combat units within their own area, is it solely under the competence and authority of municipal staffs?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Basically this was under the authority of municipal staffs, except in the case when a superior command gives an order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have another question. You have said a lot about the forward command post in Visoko. To clarify this to myself after the numerous questions of the Prosecution, I am asking you now, in the given situation that you have mentioned, did this forward command post have the authority of the main staff also over the areas of Konjic and Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA POLUTAK
utterances.text: Yes, it did, the forward command post had the authority within its area outside of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. When you want clarification about what has not been unclear to the Trial Chamber, I think you can find some other ways of doing that. This is very clear and I don't think that anybody had any doubts. But you said it was something you want to clear for yourself and it's acceptable. Now, thank you very much, Brigadier, you've been very helpful and I am sure you've been on the hot seat for quite some time. Thank you. So you're discharged. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Can we have your next witness too. Let's have your next witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: May we call in the next witness. (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Swear him, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you may take your seat, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Ms. Residovic

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir, would you please introduce yourself to the chamber by stating your full name?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: Good afternoon, my name is Husein Alic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, as I did with other witnesses, I want also to warn you of a technical issue. I will ask you questions and since we use the same language, you could quickly answer to all of my questions, but each of my questions needs to be interpreted for the honourable chamber, as well as all the others present to understand my questions and also we need to interpret the answers that you give. That's why I plea that you pay attention to the headphones on your table. We will hear the end of interpretation and from that moment on to begin with your answer to my question. Have you, Mr. Alic, understood my notice?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Also, for better understanding, I ask you to all the questions with "yes" or "no," if possible, and not to just nod your head because we need it for the transcript. Mr. Alic, will you tell us where and when you were born?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: I was born on October 5th, 1952, in Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your ethnic background and nationality?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: I am a Bosniak Muslim and my nationality is the one of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your formal education and where have you obtained it?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: Primary and high school I completed in Sarajevo, after which I went to the universities of Sarajevo and Zagreb, and I am a traffic engineer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, where were you on April 6th, 1992, when the aggression on Bosnia-Herzegovina began?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: I lived and worked in Hadzici. I was then drafted to the reserve units of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were your duties, posts, did they have anything to do with the military prior to your drafting?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: I had my own private company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, can you tell us when were you drafted to the reserve units of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: That was at the end of March or beginning of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, after that period, during 1992, have you become a member of the TO of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: Sometimes in May of 1992, I became a member of the TO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have stated that you lived in Hadzici and that you had your own private enterprise there. We've had a previous witness who was the head of the municipal assembly in Hadzici and I will, therefore, not ask you about the situation in Hadzici. I will ask you only whether at a certain point the Yugoslavia National Army took over the city and where did you, together with local populace retreat to?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: On May 9th, JNA and SDS forces took over the control of Hadzici and the population and the police forces were then moved to Pazaric and Tarcin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will also now ask you of your knowledge of regulations put into force by the state because the Chamber has seen and heard a lot of evidence about it, but I would be interested in your personal experience. In accordance with the regulations on the organisation of the TO, did you participate personally in your municipality? That is, in the formation of units of the TO.

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: In a way I did because I was a member of the MUP. And after May 9th, we were able to put together some kind of defence to prevent further advancement of the enemy and we set up a defence line and then we moved on to the formation of defence forces which demanded cooperation with the TO and the municipal staff, so in that way I did take part in the establishment of units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, as you have said, sometimes in May, you were drafted from the MUP into the TO. Did you then, together with some other people or under the task given by the municipal staff, participate in the establishing of an unit in the municipal area? If you did, can you tell us what the name of it was and where was its seat, it's headquarters?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: I took part in the forming of the so-called joint platoon of Igman and our headquarters was on Mount Igman because of its crucial strategic importance to prevent any further attacks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To clarify your position as one of the members of the TO and to set a basis for further questions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Why don't you come straight to -- (Microphone not on). Did he have any connection with TG-2? Instead of going into all the details in which you're not interested, so that he can straight away tell us what his functions were and what his connections with TG-1 were. We don't have to go into all those details.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the witness also has to understand me. I have to ask him about his functions to proceed to my following questions. I cannot directly ask him what was with the Tactical Group. I don't know if you understand, but I need a few questions to ask, so that you would see that this witness has personal knowledge of what was going on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: A person who has no personal knowledge, we know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: This will cut out a lot of evidence we are not concerned with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He has only come here to give us an idea of his connection with Delalic and the responsibility in the area of their relationship. That's why you have brought him. So all these are the peripheral areas, might not interest anyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Through what he was doing in May, we can proceed towards whether Mr. Alic had met Mr. Delalic at all and about his authority, so I just asked a few questions to give you a picture. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, before I move on to the very question I wanted the ask, I believe the Chamber has it clear, even visually speaking where the Hadzici municipality is, but, nevertheless, can you tell us how long is the line of your municipality, the border, towards the Sarajevo that was under siege? And I am asking this because this border was a place of intense fighting during the entire 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: The president of the Hadzici municipality, it is within, it is included within the municipal bounds of Sarajevo, so it couldn't be very far. It had a lot of military -- it had a military installations and the JNA occupied it. We have all been told about that. What else do you want? You think he's more informed than the president of the assembly, Hadzici, who was here two days ago before us?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I do not believe he was notified. He was on that line, on that border, so this might have interested us. But I will try to move closer to the specific questions and to skip over some ten questions I had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber will now rise and come back at 4.30 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: 4.30. --- Proceedings adjourned at 4.00 p.m. --- Proceedings reconvened at 4.30 p.m. (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I remind you, sir, that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, do you personally know that at some point in the month of May command of the Tactical Group 1 moved to the territory of your municipality and set up its headquarters there?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: Sometime in mid-May of 1992, Mustafa Polutak came to Pazaric, along with part of the command. That's when we learned that Tactical Group 1 had been established, and he was its commander, and they set up their headquarters in the school in Pazaric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this Tactical Group headquarters in the school throughout?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: No. At first it was in the school in Pazaric, and after that, after the barracks. Pazaric was taken over, it moved into the barracks. And after that, in the course of further operations, it moved to the Hotel Borik, which is where I was located also.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the basis of your knowledge, can you tell me whether the headquarters of the Tactical Group 1 throughout its -- the period of its existence, was in Pazaric, and for a period of time at Hotel Borik on Mount Igman?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, can you tell me whether in this period, while Mr. Polutak was commander, you were ever subordinate to Mr. Polutak and, if you were, when was this?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: I was subordinate, and it was also in May of 1992, along with part of my detachment, of which I was then chief of staff during the operation of the Janista (phoen) barracks, as we used to call that operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this first combat operation of Tactical Group 1, did units from Konjic also take part?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, did you take part in any other combat activity of Tactical Group 1 regarding the lifting of the siege of Sarajevo in which some of the units of Konjic took part?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: In month of June an operation was prepared which we called Tinovo Brdo, and in this operation I also took part along with the part of my detachment, as well as some units from Konjic and Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, since you were participant in these efforts to lift the siege, did Zejnil Delalic join these units, either as a member of them or as their superior commander?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: In the month of May they did not take part in it, nor did Zejnil Delalic come during the course of this operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Seid Padalovic?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: I have heard of that name. I may have met him, but I do not know him personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, can you tell me when you first met Mr. Delalic as commander of Tactical Group 1? First of all, let me ask you whether you know that Zejnil Delalic was appointed commander of Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: I learned that, I believe, in late July, when I personally met him. Until then I had heard of him, and I may have met him once in June, in Pazaric, when he was engaged in the organisation of -- starting the first train line and things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before I move onto other questions relating to Mr. Delalic, can you tell me, Mr. Alic, during the period of time that -- when Mr. Mustafa Polutak was commander of Tactical Group 1, did you take part in any other combat operations, apart from Tinovo Brdo, in trying to lift the siege?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: Yes, I did take part in the operation Brdo Strajiste. All these operations were part of preparations for the operation of the lifting of the siege of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, let me rephrase this. Did there come a time when in the area where Tactical Group 1 was involved in its operations, did in this area at some point -- was Tactical Group 2 established in that same area?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: That was also sometime in July of 1992, when the main staff deemed it necessary that Tactical Group 1, whose zone of responsibility was very large, be divided into two Tactical Groups. And at that time, in fact, the Tactical Group 2 was established. And their zones of responsibilities were separated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this combat operation in which you yourself took part with part of your detachment, and as a unit which was subordinate to Mustafa Polutak and his Tactical Group 1, what other units which were not subordinate to Mr. Polutak, to whom were they subordinate?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: They were subordinate to the municipal staff who issued orders to them, and it was normal that part of the unit be set aside for Tactical Group and the rest of them be under the command of the municipal staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the Tactical Group 2 was established, were you, Mr. Alic, appointed by the main staff to one of the duties in Tactical Group 2?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: I was appointed the chief of staff of Tactical Group 2, and commander of Tactical Group 2 was Mirsad Catic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, what was your area or what zones, so-to-speak, was the zone -- the area from which you could subordinate units to Tactical Group 2?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: The zone of responsibility of Tactical Group 2 was part of the Hadzici municipality, Mount Igman, that is the slopes, different slopes. I won't name all of them, and then the Hrasnica and Ilidza municipal staffs, Krupac and Trnovo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As chief of staff of Tactical Group 2, you certainly know whether your Tactical Group 2, during the combat activities, had under its control some combat units from the municipal staff of Hadzici?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: Yes. Of course. Tactical Group 2, the way it was conceived, did have under its command parts of the forces from the municipal staff of Hadzici, municipal staff of Ilidza or Hrasnica, and municipal staff in Trnovo, and of course the forces which were at that time deployed at Mount Igman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time of the existence of your Tactical Group, were the units which were subordinate to Hadzici municipal staff also subordinate to the Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Part of the forces of the municipal staff of Hadzici was also subordinate to the Tactical Group 1, because, in fact, half of this municipality was split in terms of the zones of responsibility between Tactical Group 1 and Tactical Group 2. And I used "half" in a very conditional way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether the remainder of the units of municipal staff of Hadzici, which, at some point, were not subordinate to either municipal -- Tactical Group 1 or Tactical Group 2, under whose command were they?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: I have already answered that the part of the units which were not subordinate to either of the Tactical Groups remained under the command of the municipal staff. Be it Hadzici, Trnovo, Ilidza, it was the same principle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, can you tell me to whom the municipal staff of the Hadzici municipality was subordinate?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: It was subordinate to the district staff in Sarajevo. For a while, while this district staff was in existence, and later when the first corps was established, it was subordinate to the first corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Given that you have spent the entire period of time in this area, did there come a time when the municipal staff in Hadzici was subordinate either to Tactical Group 1 or Tactical Group 2?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: No. That was not possible at any time. Tactical Groups 1 and 2 were established exclusively as combat formations, with specific number of troops for a specific period of time and for a specific task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, after they carried out a task for which they had been established, and I mean both in terms of Tactical Group 1 and Tactical Group 2, where did these troops that were attached to these groups go back to?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: They went to their parent unit, so-to-speak, or to their parent municipal staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this period in 1992, because you were there throughout this time, did Tactical Group 1 or Tactical Group 2 ever have fixed formations of troops for either period of time?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: We never had permanent formation. During the planning of an operation we assessed what forces we needed and, depending on whether the operation was small or large, we would use part of the forces which were subordinate to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that in late July Mr. Delalic arrived in Pazaric. Do you know -- do you personally know where the former commander, Mr. Polutak, go?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: Mr. Polutak went to Visoko to a new post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you something else, Mr. Alic. You probably know, and the court knows this, that Mr. Zejnil Delalic has no military experience as a professional soldier. Did you, Mr. Alic, have any military experience in terms of training in order to be a professional soldier?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: No. I graduated from civilian university, so-to-speak, and all my military knowledge comes from the time when I served with the JNA. However, in that period, by establishment of certain units, a person who was going to lead it, who was going to be in charge, had to be somebody from -- who was known locally, who had strong contacts. And so it was that Mr. Delalic was known as a business person, and this is why he was a commander, and his staff consisted of professional soldiers. In my case was more or less the opposite. My commander was a professional soldier and I was a local person who knew the terrain, who knew people, who had contacts and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. This would also be your opinion on why Zejnil Delalic would have been appointed to such a post; is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: In that period there was a certain amount of mistrust towards anyone who was an officer with the former JNA. Only a person of this kind, who was respected, would have been a real logical choice to assume a position of leadership, to use his contacts and lead the people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know to whom was your Tactical Group subordinate? In other words, who was the command superior to you?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: It was the supreme command of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was subordinate -- superior command to Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: It was also the supreme command of armed forces. There was no difference between Tactical Group 1 and Tactical Group 2, except by the zone of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, did there come a time when you became commander of Tactical Group 2?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: This was -- Commander Mirsad Catic was wounded in August of 1992, and then I was appointed commander of Tactical Group 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who appointed you?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: Supreme command or main staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May the witness please be shown D145/A/6, page 902.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Why are we interested in this document?
