utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Why are we interested in this document? It relates to TG2. You said that he was appointed to the supreme command. That's good enough. Why do you want to have this document before us?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So that the witness would recognise it, and it corroborates the military expert report. You instructed us to authenticate this document in this way, and I believe that this would be right way to do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: (Microphone not on) -- directed you to prove those documents which are relevant, which have a bearing on the responsibility of Mr. Zejnil Delalic. There must be a thousand documents that you can produce that have no bearing at all on the issues before us. Please be relevant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, is this document of your appointment?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: Yes, that is the pertinent document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me, at the time when you were appointed, did members of the main staff come to Mount Igman in order to prepare the attempt to lift the siege of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: Yes, two representatives of the main staff arrived there. It was Asim Dzambasovic and Dzemal Najltovic (interpreter's spelling unsure), who were supposed to coordinate the activities between Tactical Group 1 and Tactical Group 2 with respect to preparation for the lifting of siege of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, this attempt at lifting the siege of Sarajevo was conducted through this coordination, or did -- or was another command established which -- in order to command the units who would be engaged in combat?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: The main staff saw that with this coordination nothing would be accomplished, even if these were professional soldiers engaged. So it decided to establish a temporary command for this operation aimed at lifting of the siege of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, were you a member of this temporary command?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: Yes, I was a member of that command as a chief of the operations body.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether Zejnil Delalic too was a member of this temporary command?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: Yes. He was assistant commander for logistics.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Assistant commander or assistant to the commander? Was it assistant commander or assistant to the commander?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Assistant commander. May the witness please be shown Exhibit D145/A6/9, page 911.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, is this the document on appointment of the temporary command which you just spoke about?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: Yes, this is the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where is the position which you occupied, or what was your task in this command, and where is your name here?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: I think it's number 6. The head of the operations unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, at the top we see who the commander is and who the chief of staff is. Can you tell me, the other persons from this list, is there a place on the list equivalent to their place in the chain of command or hierarchy?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: In the -- on the list you have Dzemal Najltovic as a commander, and he is the most important, and then Asim Dzambasovic come after him. Then all the rest of the names does not have that hierarchical value, so the order on the list does not matter. I am the operations unit head, which, according to me, is the most important one for preparation and execution of the combat operations. But if you look at the list, in order of appearance, the security head is ahead of me, or the artillery head and the logistics head are all in front of me, and they would be minor -- of lesser importance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. According to your explanation, each of the members of this staff had his own responsibilities and authorities; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: Yes. Speaking of myself or any member of the staff, we had authorities and responsibilities within the framework of our position, mine being operation unit, and the head of communications was responsible and had the authority to the establishing of the operations, of the communication systems in the operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you were directly responsible for the conduct of combat operations, can you tell the Chamber where was Tactical Group 1 engaged, in which area, and during the operation JUG, where was engaged Tactical Group 2, in which direction or part of the zone of activity?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: TG-1 was engaged in the area Selo (phoen) Koscan, Brdo Orman, towards Hadzici. That was the ancillary direction of the planned attack, with the task of expanding the front line, distracting and taking the attention of the enemy on ourselves. And Tactical Group 2 had the task, Igman, Krupac (phoen) and further. That was the main direction of the planned operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since combat operations were your basic task, can you tell me, did Village Bjelinici in the municipality area, belong to this ancillary direction or area of activity?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: Concerning the same tasks that were referred, for example, the Village Koscan, the same should have been done to the Village Bjelinici, with the same task, and that is directing attention from the area of the main attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, under the command of the temporary command in your area, were there at that period subordinated units from other areas? That is, from areas which Tactical Group 2 did not use to subordinate units, take them from those areas?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: Yes, the most numerous unit was the one from Zenica, which was outside of our area of responsibility. And when we speak of Tactical Group 2, for example Konjic, Jablanica and so on, and we even had Vakuf. They cooperated in the operation and they were not even close to the area of the responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a person responsible for the operation, do you know that during the operation JUG, that units from Jablanica and Konjic were subordinated to Mr. Delalic as a commander of Tactical Group 1 or the person who held the authority at the ancillary direction?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: Within the framework of the JUG operation, the main direction of attack was the zone of responsibility of TG-2. For those reasons, units from Konjic and Jablanica were subordinated to the area of responsibility of TG-2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, during that operation, did you have subordinated MUP units?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: Yes, there were some under the orders of their public security stations. One of them was also a part of my security during the preparation and during the conduct of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would now move to another topic, which may be familiar to you. Since you cooperated with Mr. Delalic for a certain period of time whilst he was commander of TG-1, do you know whether Mr. Delalic at any given time was the commander of all the formations of armed forces?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: I do not understand all formations. Myself as a commander of TG-2 had authority over only over those units who were subordinate to me during the operation. The same authority had Mr. Delalic as a commander of TG-1, nothing more nor less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a chief of staff and later on the commander of TG-2, which was right behind the line of the siege, as well as the other Tactical Group, can you tell me whether you personally ever received orders of the main staff in order to transmit them to a remote municipal staff within your zone of responsibility or outside of it?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: This was usual circumstance. Communication with the main staff at the beginning relied on the messenger who would have to run over the runway and they would get killed. That was very unsafe and it would happen that we would never receive such an order. Later, we tried to communicate with the main staff through UNPROFOR, if they would permit that some of our soldiers go through the danger area and transmits such an order. But, at that time, on Bjelasnica, we had a relay, which was functioning, so we had communication with the main staff through radio communication. After I would receive such an order to transmit it to another staff, I would do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you were given such an order, were you as a soldier bound by it, did you have to fulfil it or would you reject such an order?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: How could I as a soldier reject main staff's orders? I had to carry it out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: (Microphone not on) Try and be a little bit more relevant. And let us know why we are here for the trial. It's not been helpful at all in the amount of evidence you've been leading. This is not what one expects of this witness. If he is so close to Delalic and he if was working with him for so long, we expect evidence of that relationship. Anything directed to him alone has nothing to do with this trial.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honourable Judges, these are two Tactical Groups. I wish to show whether there was a difference between this man acted and Mr. Delalic did. The next question would have been whether he knows whether Mr. Delalic were given similar orders to transmit them to other municipal staffs. If this person does not know that, then how could I ask him questions about Mr. Delalic if he doesn't know what Tactical Groups usually do?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I am listening to you over the minutes and it has been complete irrelevance to the subject matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: It's very simple. Is he aware of all the instructions and the directions in the authorisations which the supreme command had given to Mr. Delalic? Is he aware of all of them? Let him say so, then you can ask him. The supreme command may have given some different directive or authorisation to Mr. Delalic on certain other matters, so why do you ask him these questions if he cannot possibly answer?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honourable Judges, I know that the Chamber has the right to ask questions at any given moment. At their desire I will try to follow your instructions. Mr. Alic, do you know whether at any given moment, did an order from the supreme command that was transmitted to Mr. Delalic, did it change in any way his function as the commander of a Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: Such an order cannot at any moment change the nature of command post of the Tactical Group 2. This order can, due to emergency, refer the a particular task. But the basic responsibilities of a commander of TG-2 are always the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that, Mr. Alic? How often during the period of the beginning of August, when Mr. Delalic came to the Mount Igman, until you left in October, were you in the situation to be in contact with Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: I know this because we were in a daily contact, we worked, planned, organised, we even slept in the same building and we had the same common objective. We had to communicate and this was literally on a daily basis. If I received an order as a TG-2 commander, which did not directly refer to TG-1, I would only suppose that Zejnil Delalic could know of it because we are there, we share, we even share the same desk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, did you ever find out that Mr. Delalic received from the supreme staff, any authority over institutions within his area of activity?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: No, I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: How could he know everything which was communicated to Delalic by the supreme command unless he was going through all his papers all the time? He was busy looking after TG-2. Yes, they were probably together very often, but that doesn't mean that they were together all of the time or Mr. Delalic would mention every document he received from the supreme command to this witness. So why do you go into those questions? They have no bearing.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I wanted to see what this man knows because important authorisations are familiar to our companions, so if he does know, he would tell us, if not, then he would say no.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He has already answered your last question, he doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any personal knowledge that Mr. Delalic ever had any authority over prisons and was he ever given one?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: I have no personal knowledge of it and I do not know the situation where he would be given such an authority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had Mr. Delalic had such an authority, would you have been able to find that out during that period?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: I suppose that I then should have been given the same orders that TG-2 commander because we were equal in ranking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever receive any order relating to the Hadzici prison, for example?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: No, never. Tactical Group is solely a combat formation and it has no relation with institutions active within the area of responsibility of municipal staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, I will now move on to another area. You have explained to us that TG-2 had the same combat objective as the one of TG-1, that is to try to lift the siege of Sarajevo. As a commander of TG-2, as well as relating to your knowledge of the authorities of the commander of TG-1, was it important to you to receive informations and intelligence relating to the enemy?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: It is important for any commander, this is the starting point for planning of any activity, any operation. If he lacks such knowledge, I don't know how he could proceed. This is fundamental.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you personally know whether your command or a command of TG-2 had organised units for reconnaissance or intelligence gathering?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: TG-2 or TG-1 commands consisted of five or six people at the most. One of them would usually deal with intelligence and reconnaissance. This was not a body or an unit. This was usually done by the municipal staffs who had larger possibilities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As TG-2 commander, do you know whether the supreme command ever gave a directive or an order to municipal staffs binding them to provide you with such information?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: Yes, such a directive did exist, through which the main staff ordered municipal staffs to give over to commands of Tactical Groups relating to intelligence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will now ask you a hypothetical question. If a municipal staff commander or chief does not obey that order, could you have any authority over him in that respect or could you react in a completely different manner? What was your authority?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: Personally I could do nothing in relation to that commander, TO or municipal staff. I could approach the main staff or the superior commands of the municipal staff, that is the district staff, this was all that I could do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I now ask that the Prosecution Exhibit D -- no, P-224 be shown to the witness. Whilst we're waiting for the document, can you tell us, during the preparation for the operation JUG to lift off the siege of Sarajevo, due to a lack of existence of such information, were there incidents where you have penetrations done by the enemy and did that have any consequence on you performing your tasks?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: Because of those reasons, my commander, Mirsad Catic, because he lacked intelligence, he initiated a reconnaissance and a meeting dealing with the preparation of the operation and the enemy inserted a commando group, which wounded the commander and killed another member of the command staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can take a look at the document. We can see that this was dated November 14th, 1992, signed by the commander of TG-1. Have you ever seen this or a similar document during 1992?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: I have never seen this document. I am reading the text. There are overlaps with the directive from the main staff concerning tasks of reconnaissance and intelligence gathering.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have already answered that Tactical Group according to your knowledge of the time did not have different or wider authorities than the Tactical Group 2. In your knowledge, did Zejnil Delalic have such an authority in any period prior to your leaving in October?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question, I did not understand it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have said that at the time when you became commander of TG-2, Zejnil Delalic had the same authorities and responsibilities designated to that command post. I am asking you now whether the authorities that Mr. Zejnil Delalic have remain the same until you left that area in October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: Command post of a commanding function of TG-1 or TG-2 with all its responsibilities and authorities were the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, in 1992, did you leave for Konjic during the war?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: I was wounded and taken to the hospital. From that hospital directly to Mount Igman. That was when I was in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that during 1992 in Konjic in the Celebici barracks there was a prison?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: Yes, I have heard about it, but I personally have no knowledge of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This then probably means that you will affirmatively answer my following question. During 1992 then you never visited the Celebici barracks?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And since your zone of combat activity that you were present at it, during the command of Mr. Delalic, was anybody in charge of the Celebici prison subordinated to the TG-1 commander?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: A guard could be a subordinate to a commander of Tactical Group 1, but in that case he's not a guard, but a soldier. Maybe he had a different duty before that and then he moves under the command later on. That is possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any personal knowledge of anybody of that sort?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: No. I believe there was talk in the MUP unit in Konjic that one of them, I don't recall the name, was a guard. And, after that, he was a member of the MUP. And after that, he was under my command as a soldier in TG-2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This person that you refer to was under your command, not under the TG-1 command, is that the example?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC.
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And I think it's 5.30 now. We'll adjourn until tomorrow at 10.0 a.m. when cross-examination should continue. The witness can leave. You can leave. Yes, you will tomorrow. The Trial Chamber will wait when he has left. We have a few things to discuss. Yes, you can leave now. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Will you please sit down, we will have a few things. Now I think we have to discuss a very critical matter which has confronted us. The Trial Chamber has considered it in some detail. We're expecting that tomorrow the witnesses we have for this should be concluded. Even if we do not, that is the only witness list we are likely to deal with next week. But we have the intention to have the forthcoming week free because there's no need for it. We have scheduled our trial to cover that period and we expect Counsel will be able to comply. We've made the order and we are leaving a contingency plan. So that if Counsel for Delalic, as they have decided, disobey the order of the Trial Chamber, we are calling on Counsel for Mucic to make arrangements to continue to call his witnesses next week, for Monday, so that we would not have any gap within which we'll have nothing doing. Now, we are doing so most reluctantly because we feel Counsel haven't cooperated to ensure a free flow of the progress of this trial. The Trial Chamber has done everything to ensure that the trial is conducted in the interests of the accused persons themselves. I have advised Counsel for Delalic that the only alternative is to close the case of the accused person if they think that they cannot carry on next week. Because there is no way we can waive that order which we have made. Of course, perhaps, there's an escape if one is inflexible with it and if one tries to obey the orders of the Court. If Counsel for Mucic succeeds in getting his witnesses or as many of his witnesses he can call next week, then he can in this period as a Defence as a whole, take his witnesses from next week and then at the time when counsel for Defence, Delalic's Counsel, would have had all their witnesses, then you still take your own. You can still call the witnesses for the second accused. It's possible one could do it, even if it's splitting the order of presenting the Defence. It will not make a material shift in the nature of the Defence which will be presented. But, in any event, as we've said, we will not leave next week without any proceedings. That is what the Trial Chamber intends to impress on the Defence. I think we'll try also to get the victims and witnesses unit to cooperate fully with Mr. Mucic in every way in which he can succeed in getting his witnesses. If you have anything to say, let's hear it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, with all due respect for the Chamber, the interest of which is the efficiency of this proceeding which has lasted for the full 15 months now. Unfortunately, I am in no position to meet your demands within the next 72 hours for the Defence witnesses to appear before the Chamber on Monday under the assumption that the witnesses of the first accused, Mr. Zejnil Delalic, would not be at the disposal to the Chamber during the next week. And, on my behalf, I must say that work in the field, we did everything to call the witnesses in the period after the 20th of June, so we anticipated that we would start presenting evidence after the 22nd of June. But nevertheless, I can promise that the Defence will induce additional efforts to be able to meet the requests of the Honourable Chamber. But, nevertheless, I do not believe that we are going to be able to. What I am trying to say is that we will do our best. We'll try expressing our good faith to help the Chamber and make it as efficient as possible, but I do not believe, having in mind the location or dislocation of our witnesses, which are in several different places, I do not believe we are going to be able to. There's a semi-solution possibility. That would be that part of our witnesses referring to the alibi do appear during the next week, again presuming it is possible. If we are unable to do so, with all the best intentions and efforts, we will not be able to meet the requests of the Chamber, although we do not even find that the requests of the Chamber, but of mutual team work, in order to speed up the proceeding. So at the moment I exit the courtroom, my entire team will do its utmost to have the witnesses here on the Monday, the Defence witnesses for Mr. Zdravko Mucic, at least a part of them. This is all I can promise at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is the first we've ever heard of an alibi. And we certainly received no notice of such a thing under the Rules. And there's a particular requirement of Rule 67A(ii)(a). The very first we ever heard of it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: There's a problem of Rule 67 itself, which says we could not have prevented it of leading evidence even if it wasn't complied with.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I mean, the whole reason why it's there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: That's true. But the Rule itself gives an escape. I don't know why.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: But it would be gravely unfair to apply it against the Prosecution at this stage, to produce alibi, I mean this case has been going on for 15 months. They must have known they were going to have an alibi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: If you look at Rule 67 B, it's very clearly stated there. I have always felt that was funny, but that's what the Rule is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Well, it's discretionary, Your Honour. In my submission, you exercise that discretion against us. Having regard for the fact, this case has gone for 15 months, it would be extraordinarily unfair. To raise an alibi at this stage is, frankly, outrageous.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Have we anything else to say about the matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The Prosecution will not be ready to respond to an alibi next week if there's an alibi to be raised. And we specifically ask that an order be made now that they comply with Rule 67 in relation to giving an alibi notice. I mean, it's extraordinary that Counsel could stand up at this stage after all the time this trial has been going and to mention an alibi for the very first time. We'll be making a motion, Your Honours -- to Your Honours for such an order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: In the criminal case the accused has many privileges which the Prosecution doesn't enjoy.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: But, Your Honours, in most jurisdictions. This is not one of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: And that's why I mentioned the Rule itself. I was surprised when it was insisted on giving that provision of Rule 67B.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I complied with certain circumstances where some sort of provisions of this may be necessary. But of a trial that's been going for 15 months, it's to suggest that they didn't know about (a) the Rule, and (b) the need to provide notice and (c), the necessity to inform of us an alibi is extraordinary and just unbelievable, frankly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I don't know why that provision is there, but it was insisted on by the Rules Committee and they felt it has to be there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: But, Your Honours, it's not mandatory for you to exercise it in that way. There may be an exception which the Chamber may wish to rely on at some stage, which it is there for. But it's an exception to the Rule. The Rule is that alibi evidence is to be provided, and there's a very good reason for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The Rule has stated that what is said. That by itself does not deprive the accused from giving evidence of alibi, which means they actually knew this -- there might be cases where other people might not even give notice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I do not know what defence Mr. Olujic is going to produce, but maybe the passport of Mr. Mucic indicate when he was away, and when he was not away, and I think you had a copy of the passport.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: We were not given an alibi notice, if Your Honour pleases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Not an alibi, his passport.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I don't know, and I can't possibly contemplate what the alibi would be, and I note that Rule B, which Your Honour is referring to, relates to the accused himself testifying, and we certainly have no objection to the accused testifying. It's calling witnesses that we are objecting to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: In fact, one of the Defence witnesses, a gentleman from Vienna, has already spoken about the frequent visits of Mr. Mucic to Vienna where they dined together, they lived together. One of the Defence witnesses already said that -- I think it was the witness from Vienna, who stated to have prepared a video for the benefit of Mr. Delalic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That reinforces my position, because they must have known about their alibi far in advance of this trial and be well in a position to give us notice under the Rules. And paragraph B relates, Your Honours, to the defendant himself testifying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We shall follow the Rules. Don't worry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Mr. Olujic, any replies to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Thank you for your assistance. Because the Trial Chamber is fully aware of the Rules, and in referring to Rule 67, and my colleague who calls outrageous the fact that he did not receive the notice of alibi to them. On 7th March 1997 the Defence provided a list of persons to whom the accused -- my client will call for his -- in his Defence. And it is terrible if the Prosecution is not aware of it. And we have duly registered it with the Tribunal and it has been there since 7 March 1997. It has been initiated by my colleague, Mr. Tapuskovic, who was the lead counsel at the time. We have a copy of that submission and so should the Prosecution. And if they refer to it, they will glean from it that our client is using the alibi Defence, and then, in addition to that we do have Rule 67, which Your Honours have amply clarified. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, on behalf of the Defence of Mr. Zejnil Delalic, I thank you for your understanding of the problems facing the Defence in trying to call witnesses. I believe that you know, and I believe that your decision, which takes into account our problems, is also consistent with our efforts to comply with the decisions of this Court, and also with our efforts to bring to this Trial Chamber those witnesses who will not duplicate the evidence. And also given the fact that some of the witnesses that we were trying to call do have real scheduling conflicts. The person that we just called was on an official business trip in Austria. He interrupted his trip to come here. We will continue to make all the effort that we can, and should we identify another witness whom we can call for next week, we will immediately inform you of that. Thank you for understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I must apologise. It looks as though we have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You don't have to. You know how communication -- and these things do happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: It happens. The court has thousands of pages. One can miss.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I apologise sincerely to Mr. Olujic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic, I think we are very certain that we had this period laid out for your witnesses, and they have been there since May. We've carried on having your witnesses, and we thought perhaps this last lap should not have given us any difficulty at all. And we'll have to carry on. Especially with the fact that you are unable to bring your witnesses -- we'll carry on, do it's best. We've tried to accommodate everyone, and we continue to do so, but if you are unable, then accused with similar status on Defence -- then we concluded this in the way we designed it. I think this is all we have to say. As I say, we'll try and impress on the victims and witnesses you need to do your best to accommodate your demand. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
